### D-DATA-08

keyed by the canonical absolute path; messages unchanged

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| relative local-path repos (`repo: ../tools`) share one cache entry across projects | keyed by the canonical absolute path; messages unchanged |

##### Rationale

pre-commit keys its `repos` table by the `repo:` string verbatim (`db_repo_name`, `store.py:125-171`). Two projects
whose configs both say `repo: ../tools`, with `rev: HEAD` (or the same tag name), share one row: the second project
silently runs the first project's hooks — different code than its config names, from another directory. The same
happens to one project moved or cloned twice.

snp derives repository keys only through `RepoId::from_config(repo, project_root)` (ADR-070): a `repo:` value that
names an existing local directory (relative values resolved against the project root, `os.path.isdir` semantics) is
identified by its `realpath` (`abs:` + path bytes in the blake3 key), every other value by the string verbatim. gc
resolves tracked configs against their recorded project roots (ADR-075). Messages keep the verbatim string:
`[INFO] Initializing environment for ../tools.`.

Safe: each project runs the hooks its own config names. The cost is one extra clone per distinct directory, which is
what the configs ask for.

##### Examples

Recorded with pre-commit 4.6.2 on CPython 3.12.3 (a venv built from the hash lock `xtask/oracle/requirements-pc462.txt`); `<W>` is the scratch root, `<store>` the store directory.

Projects `one/proj` and `two/proj`, each with `repo: ../tools`, `rev: HEAD` and a hook `which` whose entry echoes the
project name of its `tools` directory; `run --all-files` in `one/proj`, then in `two/proj`
(`tests/differential/divergences/D-DATA-08.yaml`). pre-commit 4.6.2 in `two/proj`, exit 0:

```text
[WARNING] The 'rev' field of repo '../tools' appears to be a mutable reference (moving tag / branch).  Mutable references are never updated after first install and are not supported.  See https://pre-commit.com/#using-the-latest-version-for-a-repository for more details.  Hint: `pre-commit autoupdate` often fixes this.
which....................................................................Passed
- hook id: which
- duration: 0s

tools of project one

```

snp in `two/proj`, exit 0 (its own `tools`, newly initialised):

```text
[WARNING] The 'rev' field of repo '../tools' appears to be a mutable reference (moving tag / branch).  Mutable references are never updated after first install and are not supported.  See https://pre-commit.com/#using-the-latest-version-for-a-repository for more details.  Hint: `pre-commit autoupdate` often fixes this.
[INFO] Initializing environment for ../tools.
which....................................................................Passed
- hook id: which
- duration: 0s

tools of project two

```

Unit coverage: `crates/snp-store/tests/support/behaviour.rs::repo_id_from_config_uses_the_project_root`.

### D-DATA-09

UTF-8 always, each line's original EOL kept, atomic replace keeping the mode

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| migrate-config/autoupdate read/write with the locale encoding and rewrite CRLF files as LF; non-atomic writes | UTF-8 always, each line's original EOL kept, atomic replace keeping the mode |

##### Rationale

`migrate_config` reads with universal newlines and writes with `open(config_file, 'w')`: on POSIX a CRLF file that
needs migration is rewritten with LF everywhere, on Windows every line gets CRLF; the encoding is the locale's;
and the write truncates in place, so an interrupted write leaves a truncated config (01 §10, D-CRASH-25).

snp keeps the bytes it does not migrate: the text is decoded as strict UTF-8 without newline translation, every
rewrite splices only the touched scalar (or inserts the `repos:` line with the file's own line ending), so each
line keeps its `\n` or `\r\n`. The new bytes are handed to the caller, which writes them atomically (temp file in
the same directory, fsync, rename) keeping the file's mode. When nothing needs migrating the file is untouched in
both tools.

##### Examples

Input (CRLF endings):

```
-   repo: local␍␊
    hooks:␍␊
    -   id: x␍␊
        name: x␍␊
        entry: x␍␊
        language: system␍␊
        stages: [commit]␍␊
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 on Linux writes `repos:\n-   repo: local\n …        stages: [pre-commit]\n` (every ending LF).
snp writes `repos:\r\n-   repo: local\r\n …        stages: [pre-commit]\r\n` (every ending kept, the inserted
line uses the file's CRLF). Both print `Configuration has been migrated.`.

### D-DATA-10

the line keeps its \r (DEV-PY-1)

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| `autoupdate --freeze` rewrites a CRLF `rev:` line with LF (mixed endings) | the line keeps its `\r` (DEV-PY-1) |

##### Rationale

`REV_LINE_RE` ends with `(.*)(\r?\n)$`; because `.` matches `\r`, a CRLF line's `\r` lands in group 5 (the
comment) and group 6 is always `\n` (15 §A4.6). When `--freeze` replaces the comment with `  # frozen: <tag>`, or an
un-freeze drops a `# frozen:` comment, the `\r` goes with it: the rewritten `rev:` line ends in LF amid CRLF
lines, a mixed-ending file that editors and `git diff` flag on every autoupdate.

snp appends the `\r` back when the comment it replaced ended with one (DEV-PY-1). Lines whose comment is kept are
byte-identical to pre-commit's (the `\r` is still in the kept group 5), and LF files are unaffected.

##### Examples

`    rev: v1  # note␍␊` updated with `--freeze` to `bbbb…` (tag `v2`):

pre-commit 4.6.2 writes `    rev: bbbb…  # frozen: v2␊`; snp writes `    rev: bbbb…  # frozen: v2␍␊`.
Un-freezing `    rev: bbbb…  # frozen: v1␍␊` to `v2`: pre-commit `    rev: v2␊`, snp `    rev: v2␍␊`.

### D-DATA-11

GIT_DIFF_OPTS removed for the stash diff-index

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| `GIT_DIFF_OPTS=--unified=0` makes the stash patch unrestorable (hazard a) | `GIT_DIFF_OPTS` removed for the stash `diff-index` |

##### Rationale

`GIT_DIFF_OPTS=--unified=<n>` changes the context of every patch git prints, `diff-index` included (02 G.0 hazard (a),
observed on 4.6.2). With `--unified=0` the stash patch has no context lines; `git apply` refuses zero-context hunks
unless `--unidiff-zero` is given, so both applies fail, the rollback does not help, and pre-commit exits 3 with the
user's unstaged changes only in the patch file — on every commit with unstaged changes, as long as the variable is
exported (some users set it for their own `git diff`).

snp removes `GIT_DIFF_OPTS` from the environment of the stash's `diff-index` only (02 G.7 row 2). The modification
detection diff (`git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --ignore-submodules`) keeps it — it is compared only for
equality, so it is harmless there — and hooks still see it.

Why it is safe: the variable has no other effect on that call; on every path where pre-commit's stash works, the
patch is byte-identical (the default context is 3 lines either way).

##### Examples

```text
$ GIT_DIFF_OPTS=--unified=0 pre-commit run      # unstaged change + a non-conflicting hook fix
[WARNING] Unstaged files detected.
[INFO] Stashing unstaged files to /s/patch1791403656-1781218.
fixer....................................................................Failed
…
[WARNING] Stashed changes conflicted with hook auto-fixes... Rolling back fixes...
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('/usr/bin/git', '-c', 'core.autocrlf=false', 'apply', '--whitespace=nowarn', '/s/patch1791403656-1781218')
return code: 1
…
$ GIT_DIFF_OPTS=--unified=0 snp run
[WARNING] Unstaged files detected.
[INFO] Stashing unstaged files to /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218.
fixer....................................................................Failed
…
[INFO] Restored changes from /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218.
```

Proof: `crates/snp-stash/tests/behaviour/guard.rs::hazard_a_git_diff_opts_unified_zero_is_restorable`,
`behaviour/stage_fixed.rs::binary_patch_and_unified_zero_are_restorable_with_staged_fixes`; the scenario
`tests/differential/divergences/D-DATA-11.yaml`.

### D-DATA-12

--no-renames on the ITA query

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| an intent-to-add file paired as a rename is missed ⇒ restore fails and a deletion is lost (hazard b) | `--no-renames` on the ITA query |

##### Rationale

`git.intent_to_add_files` (`git.py:146-151`) lists intent-to-add files as `--diff-filter=A` entries of `git diff`.
With rename detection on (`diff.renames=true`, git's default), an intent-to-add file whose content resembles a tracked
file deleted in the worktree is reported as a rename (`R`), not an addition, so it is missed (02 G.0 hazard (b),
observed on 4.6.2). It then stays in the index as an intent-to-add entry: the stash patch contains it as a new file,
the checkout leaves it in place, every `git apply` fails with `already exists in working directory`, pre-commit exits
3, and the user's unstaged deletion is lost from the worktree (it exists only in the patch).

snp adds `--no-renames` to that one query (02 G.7 row 1): additions are then always reported as additions. The other
`--name-only` queries keep git's (and the user's) rename settings where they change pre-commit's output (02 G.0
item 9).

Why it is safe: on every repository where the query does not pair a rename, its output is byte-identical; where it
does, pre-commit loses data and snp does not.

##### Examples

```text
$ git rm --cached -q a.txt; mv a.txt b.txt; git add -N b.txt   # (or: delete a.txt, create a similar b.txt, add -N)
$ pre-commit run
[INFO] Stashing unstaged files to /s/patch1791403656-1781218.
…
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('/usr/bin/git', '-c', 'core.autocrlf=false', 'apply', '--whitespace=nowarn', '/s/patch1791403656-1781218')
return code: 1
stdout: (none)
stderr:
    error: b.txt: already exists in working directory
$ snp run
[WARNING] Unstaged intent-to-add files detected.
[WARNING] Unstaged files detected.
…
[INFO] Restored changes from /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218.
```

Proof: `crates/snp-stash/tests/behaviour/guard.rs::hazard_b_intent_to_add_paired_as_a_rename`; the scenario
`tests/differential/divergences/D-DATA-12.yaml`.

### D-DATA-13

per-worktree lock (nested runs exempt via token only while the lock is held), durable journal + git-dir pointer, patch re-verified before the checkout, next-run recovery notice…

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| two concurrent runs in one worktree can stash over each other; a killed run leaves no recovery hint | per-worktree lock (nested runs exempt via token only while the lock is held), durable journal + git-dir pointer, patch re-verified before the checkout, next-run recovery notice on stderr (`git apply --3way`) |

##### Rationale

pre-commit's stash has no mutual exclusion and no record. Two runs in one worktree (an IDE's commit next to a
terminal one; git ≥ 2.55 parallel hooks) can both `diff-index` the same unstaged changes: the second sees the first's
clean checkout, and whichever restores last decides what the user gets back. A run killed between the checkout and the
restore (SIGKILL, OOM, power loss, a crashed IDE) leaves the work only in `patch<ts>-<pid>`, the file is written
without `fsync`, and nothing ever mentions it again. An editor autosave between `diff-index` and the checkout is
discarded silently.

snp adds, with no change to any byte pre-commit prints on a working path (ARCHITECTURE §4, ADR-016/026/067):

* a per-worktree lock `<git_dir>/snp-stash.lock` (linked worktrees have their own); a second run waits up to
  `SNP_STASH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (60 s) with one stderr notice (D-DIAG-04), then fails with a `FatalError`; a nested run (a
  hook running snp) is exempt only when its `_SNP_STASH_LOCK` (D-EXT-04) equals the token in the lock file **and** the
  lock is really held — a stale token exempts nobody;
* the patch is created `create_new` 0600 (two runs with the same second and pid get `-1`, `-2` …), `fsync`ed, and
  re-verified by a second `diff-index` digest right before the checkout (an autosave is caught: the patch is
  rewritten, at most 3 times, else `FatalError: snp: unstaged files kept changing while stashing; nothing was
  modified`);
* a journal `<store>/patches/run-<pid>-<rand>.snp-journal` and a pointer `<git_dir>/snp-stash.journal`, written before
  every mutation (fsynced for the data-protecting states), deleted when the run is done;
* the next run in the worktree (any store: the pointer is in the git dir) prints, on stderr, for every orphaned
  journal: `snp: an earlier run was interrupted before it restored your unstaged changes; they are saved in <patch>
  (index tree <tree>). Restore with: git --literal-pathspecs checkout <tree> -- <patch paths…> && git apply --3way
  <patch> && git --literal-pathspecs reset -q <tree> -- <patch paths…> <stage_fixed paths…>`. After the stash
  checkout the worktree holds only staged content and hook edits in the patch's paths (the user's work is in the
  patch), so they are first put back to their stash-time contents — otherwise `git apply` refuses a path a hook or
  `stage_fixed` touched (`does not match index`); the final reset gives back the pre-run index (the `--3way` apply
  stages, and `stage_fixed` may have staged fixes). Paths are literal pathspecs. A long list (more than 64 paths or
  4096 bytes) or an unparseable patch uses `git read-tree <tree> && git checkout-index -f -a && git apply --3way
  <patch> && git read-tree <tree>`. Intent-to-add paths the run cleared are re-added last
  (`&& git --literal-pathspecs add --intent-to-add -- <paths…>`). A run killed after clearing intent-to-add entries
  but with no patch at risk (before the patch, or after the restore) gets one notice `snp: an earlier run was
  interrupted before it re-added its intent-to-add files. Restore with: git --literal-pathspecs add --intent-to-add
  -- <paths…>`, printed once. Nothing is ever applied automatically. (The checkout discards hook edits — and any
  later edits — in the patch's paths, as pre-commit's own rollback does.)

Why it is safe: stdout and exit codes of every run that works in pre-commit are unchanged; the only visible
differences are waiting (instead of corrupting a concurrent run) and stderr notices about work pre-commit would
silently strand.

##### Examples

```text
# a second `snp run` while the first is inside its hooks
$ snp run
snp: waiting for another snp run in this worktree…
… (after SNP_STASH_LOCK_TIMEOUT)
An error has occurred: FatalError: snp: another snp run in this worktree still holds /r/.git/snp-stash.lock after 60 s; set SNP_STASH_LOCK_TIMEOUT (seconds, at most 3600) to wait longer

# the run after a `kill -9` during the hooks (stderr)
snp: an earlier run was interrupted before it restored your unstaged changes; they are saved in /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218 (index tree 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904). Restore with: git --literal-pathspecs checkout 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 -- foo && git apply --3way /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218 && git --literal-pathspecs reset -q 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 -- foo
```

Proof: `crates/snp-stash/tests/behaviour/{guard,recovery}.rs` (lock, nested token, stale token, autosave, patch
names, pointer with another store), `tests/driver.rs::kill_9_at_every_transition_…` (the next run prints exactly
`Unrestored::hint`, and the hinted commands restore the work); the scenario
`tests/differential/divergences/D-DATA-13.yaml`.

### D-DATA-14

rewrites deduplicated by YAML node

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| migrate-config doubles the rewrite of an aliased `stages` list (`[pre-commitpre-commit]`) | rewrites deduplicated by YAML node |

##### Rationale

`_migrate_composed` collects the scalar nodes its matchers reach and splices each replacement at the node's marks.
A YAML alias is the same node object as its anchor, so a stage list reached twice (`default_stages: &s [commit]`
and `stages: *s`) is rewritten twice at the same offsets: the second splice lands on the first one's output and
the file becomes `default_stages: &s [pre-commitpre-commit]`, an invalid stage that breaks the config (01 §10).

snp's composer gives aliases the anchor's `NodeId` (ADR-002), and the rewrites are deduplicated by node before
splicing, so the anchored value is rewritten exactly once — which is also what every alias then sees. The
dedupe is a bitmap over the dense node ids, linear in the number of rewrites (a `Vec::contains` scan made a
320k-item `default_stages` list take ≈ 35 s).

The same hazard has a second form: pre-commit replaces a node from its *start mark*, which lies before the
node's properties, so a rewritten scalar loses its `!tag` and its `&anchor` (`&k sha: v1` → `rev: v1`). Losing
the anchor makes every later `*k` an undefined alias, and the migrated file no longer loads. snp keeps each
`&anchor` (with the whitespace after it) in front of the replacement; the `!tag` is dropped exactly as in
pre-commit (`[!!str commit]` → `[pre-commit]`, byte-identical), since the rewritten value is a plain string
either way.

##### Examples

```yaml
default_stages: &s [commit]
repos:
-   repo: local
    hooks:
    -   id: x
        name: x
        entry: x
        language: system
        stages: *s
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 `migrate-config` writes `default_stages: &s [pre-commitpre-commit]` (exit 0; every later command
fails validation). snp writes `default_stages: &s [pre-commit]` and leaves `stages: *s` as is.

```yaml
repos:
-   repo: https://x/r
    &k sha: v1
    hooks: []
x: *k
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 writes `    rev: v1` and leaves `x: *k` (exit 0; the next load fails with `=====> found undefined
alias`). snp writes `    &k rev: v1`, and the file still loads.

### D-DATA-15

block scalars rewritten safely

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| migrate-config turns a folded `language: >-\n  python_venv` into invalid YAML | block scalars rewritten safely |

##### Rationale

`_preserve_style` writes the replacement as `{style}{new}{style}`, where `style` is the node's PyYAML style: `'`
and `"` for quoted scalars, but `|` and `>` for block scalars. A folded `language: >-\n    python_venv` therefore
becomes `language: >python>` — not YAML — and the next command fails to parse the config (01 §10).

snp rewrites a block scalar as the plain scalar `python` (or `pre-commit`, …) followed by exactly the line breaks
and indentation the block's token ended with, so the surrounding lines are unchanged and the value is what
pre-commit meant. Quoted and plain scalars keep pre-commit's replacement byte for byte.

##### Examples

```yaml
repos:
-   repo: local
    hooks:
    -   id: x
        name: x
        entry: x
        language: >-
            python_venv
        files: a
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 writes `        language: >python>        files: a` (invalid YAML). snp writes
`        language: python\n        files: a\n`.

### D-DATA-16

end of file treated as a line end; comments kept

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| autoupdate: a config without a final newline triggers a full PyYAML re-dump that drops all comments | end of file treated as a line end; comments kept |

##### Rationale

`REV_LINE_RE` requires a newline, so a `rev:` on the last line of a file without a final newline never matches;
the rev-line count then differs from the repo count and autoupdate re-dumps the whole file through PyYAML
(`yaml_dump(yaml_load(original))`), dropping every comment and reformatting every line (03 §11.3; observed with a
`# keep me` header). Editors that omit the final newline are common.

snp matches the unterminated last line as if it ended with `\n` and writes it back without one. Every other file
gets pre-commit's rewrite; the re-dump fallback stays for configs whose rev lines really cannot be located
(flow style, `rev:` at column 0, extra `rev:` keys).

##### Examples

```
# keep me
repos:
-   repo: a
    hooks: []
    rev: v1  # c        ← no final newline
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 `autoupdate` (to `v2`) writes `repos:\n-   repo: a\n    hooks: []\n    rev: v2\n` — the header and
the comment are gone. snp writes the file unchanged except `    rev: v2  # c` (still no final newline).

### D-DATA-17

a stash that would be non-empty on git < 2.19 is refused before any mutation: An error has occurred: FatalError: git <V> cannot stash intent-to-add files safely; snp requires git 2.19.0 or newer…

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.2)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| git < 2.19 does not report intent-to-add files: a stash with an ITA file fails after the rollback (`already exists in working directory`, exit 3), leaving the unstaged work only in the patch (02 G.3); runs without a stash work | a stash that would be non-empty on git < 2.19 is refused before any mutation: `An error has occurred: FatalError: git <V> cannot stash intent-to-add files safely; snp requires git 2.19.0 or newer to stash unstaged changes (found <git>).` (exit 1); every run that needs no stash works as in pre-commit |

##### Rationale

Before git 2.19, `git diff` does not show intent-to-add entries as new files, so `git.intent_to_add_files` returns
nothing (02 G.3, observed on 2.18.5). An intent-to-add file then ends up in the stash patch as an addition while it
stays in the index; the checkout leaves it, both applies fail with `already exists in working directory`, the
rollback does not help, and pre-commit exits 3 with the user's unstaged changes only in the patch.

snp cannot detect intent-to-add files on such a git either, so it does not try (ADR-063): when `diff-index` shows
unstaged changes on git < 2.19, snp refuses before writing a patch or touching the worktree. A run with nothing to
stash (`diff-index` clean or the CRLF quirk) proceeds exactly as in pre-commit, so commits without unstaged changes
keep working on old git.

Why it is safe: K5 holds (a refusal is non-zero, like pre-commit's crash on the affected path); nothing is mutated; the
message names the fix (upgrade git). The refusal also covers unstaged changes without intent-to-add files, which
pre-commit stashes correctly on 2.18 — a deliberate, documented over-approximation, because snp cannot tell the two
apart without the git feature that is missing.

##### Examples

```text
$ /opt/git-2.18.5/bin/git add -N n.txt; echo change >> b.txt   # an ITA file and an unstaged change
$ pre-commit run
[WARNING] Unstaged files detected.
[INFO] Stashing unstaged files to /s/patch1791403656-1781218.
…
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('/opt/git-2.18.5/bin/git', '-c', 'core.autocrlf=false', 'apply', '--whitespace=nowarn', '/s/patch1791403656-1781218')
…
    error: n.txt: already exists in working directory
$ snp run
An error has occurred: FatalError: git 2.18.5 cannot stash intent-to-add files safely; snp requires git 2.19.0 or newer to stash unstaged changes (found /opt/git-2.18.5/bin/git).
```

Proof: `crates/snp-stash/tests/behaviour/guard.rs::old_git_refuses_a_non_empty_stash_before_any_mutation` (the
refusal comes before any patch or checkout; a clean run proceeds); the scenario
`tests/differential/divergences/D-DATA-17.yaml` runs on the CI git 2.18.5 container.

## 5.3 SEC — security

### D-SEC-01

sanitized-or-hashed env dir names; deletion contained in the repo's envs/

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| `language_version: ../../x` (or an absolute path) makes the install step delete arbitrary directories; Windows `C:` versions break | sanitized-or-hashed env dir names; deletion contained in the repo's `envs/` |

##### Rationale

pre-commit names an environment `os.path.normpath(os.path.join(prefix, f'{ENVIRONMENT_DIR}-{language_version}'))`
(`lang_base.py:90-91`). `language_version` comes from the config: `..` components escape the store entry, and the
install step removes the directory it computed — first `rmtree(venv)` when it exists (a "partial previous install"),
then `clean_path_on_failure` when the install fails (`repository.py:72-89`). A config in a cloned repository can thus
delete any directory the user can write (04b §5.1, verified); an absolute version nests directories, and a Windows
`C:` version breaks the path.

snp's `Store::env_dir` (ADR-009) uses `<ENV_DIR>-<version>` only when the version matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,64}$`,
is not `.`/`..` and cannot alias another name on the filesystem (no trailing `.`, which Win32 strips, so `3.12.` would
open `3.12`; on Windows and macOS, whose default filesystems fold case, no upper-case ASCII, so `3.12A` and `3.12a` never
share an environment); anything else becomes `<ENV_DIR>-h<hex16(blake3(version))>`. The name is always one component
directly inside `<repo>/envs`, and environment removal goes through `remove_tree_within(env_dir, <repo>/envs)`
(fd-relative on Unix, never following a symlink). Every real version string (`python3.12`, `3.12.1`, `system`,
`default`, `22.11.0`) keeps its readable name.

Safe: the store is private to snp (FD-2), so the directory name is not observable except in error texts that quote it;
the install itself receives the original `language_version` and fails or succeeds exactly as before.

##### Examples

Recorded with pre-commit 4.6.2 on CPython 3.12.3 (a venv built from the hash lock `xtask/oracle/requirements-pc462.txt`); `<W>` is the scratch root, `<store>` the store directory.

A local `language: python` hook with `language_version: ../../../../sec01-victim`, where `<W>/sec01-victim/keep.txt`
exists next to the store (`<W>/store`). pre-commit 4.6.2, `run --all-files`, exit 3:

```text
[INFO] Initializing environment for local.
[INFO] Installing environment for local.
[INFO] Once installed this environment will be reused.
[INFO] This may take a few minutes...
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('<venv>/bin/python', '-mvirtualenv', '<W>/sec01-victim', '-p', '../../../../sec01-victim')
return code: 1
stdout:
    RuntimeError: failed to find interpreter for Builtin discover of python_spec='../../../../sec01-victim'
stderr: (none)
Check the log at <W>/store/pre-commit.log
```

and `<W>/sec01-victim` (with `keep.txt`) **has been deleted**. snp computes `<store>/repos-v1/<key>/envs/py_env-h<16
hex>`; the install fails on the unusable interpreter request the same way (exit 3), and nothing outside `envs/` is
touched. The scenario (`tests/differential/divergences/D-SEC-01.yaml`) climbs to `/` and back down into the worktree,
so the oracle deletes a committed directory and the tree comparison shows the difference.

Unit coverage: `crates/snp-store/tests/support/behaviour.rs::env_dir_names_are_sanitized_or_hashed` and the
`store_env_dir_name` fuzz target.

### D-SEC-05

installers and owned repos get pre-commit's no_git_env allow-list

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| installers and snp-owned repo operations inherit `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` (index corruption in linked worktrees; autoupdate writes partial-clone config into the user's repo — hazard c) | installers and owned repos get pre-commit's `no_git_env` allow-list |

##### Rationale

git exports `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` while it runs hooks, and shells export `GIT_DIR` for
dotfile setups and `git --git-dir` wrappers. pre-commit strips them for its store clone (`git.no_git_env`,
`git.py:27-48`) but not for `autoupdate`'s temporary repository after `init_repo` (`autoupdate.py:40-72`: `config`,
`fetch`, `describe`, `tag`, `rev-parse`, `show`, `checkout` run with the full environment), nor for language
installers (`pip`, `npm`, `go install` building packages with git). With `GIT_DIR` exported, `git -C <tmp> config
extensions.partialClone true` writes into the **user's** repository, the following `fetch` from `origin` fails, and
the user is left with `repositoryformatversion = 1`, `extensions.partialClone = true` and a promisor remote that
changes how every later fetch of their repository behaves (02 G.3 hazard c). In a linked worktree an installer that
runs git with the hook's `GIT_INDEX_FILE` writes the wrong index (prek #2505).

snp runs **every** git call on a repository it owns — store clones, deps variants, autoupdate, the try-repo shadow —
with `no_git_env(base)`: pre-commit's own allow-list (every `GIT_*` variable dropped except `GIT_EXEC_PATH`,
`GIT_SSH`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`KEY_*`/`VALUE_*`,
`GIT_HTTP_PROXY_AUTHMETHOD`, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL`, `GIT_ASKPASS`; names upper-cased on Windows like CPython's
`os.environ` copy, ADR-074), plus `core.fsmonitor=` and `core.useBuiltinFSMonitor=false` appended through
`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` (an existing count is extended, a malformed one left alone). The argv stays pre-commit's (error
texts are unchanged); only the environment of calls on snp's own repositories differs, and only where pre-commit
reads or writes the wrong repository. User-repository calls keep the full environment (parity, 02 G.6).

##### Examples

A hooks repository with tags `v1.0.0`, `v2.0.0`; the user repository's config pins `rev: v1.0.0`; the shell exports
`GIT_DIR=<user>/.git`; `pre-commit autoupdate`.

pre-commit 4.6.2 (oracle `pc462-py312`, git 2.43.0), exit **3**, stdout:

```
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('/usr/bin/git', '-c', 'core.useBuiltinFSMonitor=false', '-C', '/tmp/tmpsblpeqct', 'fetch', 'origin', 'HEAD', '--quiet', '--filter=blob:none', '--tags')
return code: 128
stdout: (none)
stderr:
    fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository
    fatal: Could not read from remote repository.

    Please make sure you have the correct access rights
    and the repository exists.
Check the log at <store>/pre-commit.log
```

and the user's `.git/config` afterwards:

```diff
-	repositoryformatversion = 0
+	repositoryformatversion = 1
+[extensions]
+	partialClone = true
+[remote "origin"]
+	promisor = true
+	partialclonefilter = blob:none
```

snp: `[<hooks>] updating v1.0.0 -> v2.0.0`, the config is rewritten, exit **0**; the user's `.git/config` is
byte-identical before and after.

Regression tests: `crates/snp-git/tests/behaviour/hazards.rs`
`hazard_c_git_dir_never_redirects_autoupdate_into_the_user_repo` (real git, `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/
`GIT_INDEX_FILE` exported; the user repository is unchanged), `crates/snp-git/tests/behaviour/owned.rs`
`owned_env_is_sanitized_and_carries_the_fsmonitor_injection` (the environment of every owned call) and the catalog
row T10-GIT-12 (`no_git_env`).

### D-SEC-06

one retry with the other `--object-format` after `mismatched algorithms`

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| clones fail when the user's git defaults to SHA-256 objects (hazard d) | one retry with the other `--object-format` after `mismatched algorithms` |

##### Rationale

`store.clone` creates the clone with `git init --template=` and then fetches (`store.py:185-210`). `git init` picks
the object format from the user's configuration (`init.defaultObjectFormat`, git ≥ 2.49; the default of Git 3.0), a
fetch cannot change it, and git refuses to fetch between formats: `fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha256;
server sha1`. With a SHA-256 default every SHA-1 hook repository — practically all of them — fails to clone (exit 3
on every run), and the same happens the other way round when a SHA-256 hook repository is used from a SHA-1 default.
`GIT_DEFAULT_HASH` cannot cause it (`no_git_env` strips it), so only the configuration matters (02 G.3 hazard d).

snp runs pre-commit's exact sequence first (identical argv, identical errors in every case that already works). When
it fails and git's stderr reports the mismatch (`mismatched algorithms`, or — in a translated message — both
algorithm names, the last one being the server's), and git supports `init --object-format` (≥ 2.29), the clone
directory is emptied and the whole sequence runs once more after `git init --template= --object-format=<server's
format>`. A second failure is reported as is. Nothing else changes: the retry only ever turns an exit-3 clone failure
into a working clone of exactly the requested revision.

##### Examples

A SHA-256 hook repository (`git init --object-format=sha256`, one commit `<64-hex>`); the user's git has the default
SHA-1 object format; `.pre-commit-config.yaml` pins `rev: <64-hex>`; `pre-commit run --all-files`.

pre-commit 4.6.2 (oracle `pc462-py312`, git 2.43.0), exit **3**, stdout:

```
[INFO] Initializing environment for <root>/hooks.
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('/usr/bin/git', 'fetch', 'origin', '--tags')
return code: 128
stdout: (none)
stderr:
    fatal: mismatched algorithms: client sha1; server sha256
Check the log at <store>/pre-commit.log
```

snp: `[INFO] Initializing environment for <root>/hooks.`, the clone is retried as SHA-256 and the hook runs (`x…
Passed`), exit **0**. The mirror case (a user `init.defaultObjectFormat=sha256` against SHA-1 hook repositories,
git ≥ 2.49) is the same code path; CI's latest-git job covers it.

Regression tests: `crates/snp-git/tests/behaviour/hazards.rs` `hazard_d_object_format_mismatch_is_retried_once` (real
git: a SHA-256 upstream cloned with a SHA-1 default ends up a SHA-256 clone at the requested commit; the upstream is
unchanged) and the unit test `owned::tests::object_format_from_mismatch_message` (English and translated messages).

### D-SEC-07

With `PATH` unset or empty, snp's activation patches put no empty entry (the current directory) on `PATH`.

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| unset `PATH` ⇒ activation patches produce `"<bin>:"` (cwd on PATH) | no trailing separator |

##### Rationale

Every environment language of pre-commit 4.6.2 activates its environment with an `envcontext` patch of the form
`('PATH', (bin_dir, os.pathsep, Var('PATH')))` (`languages/python.py:60`, `node.py:56`, `golang.py:73,82`,
`rust.py:53`, `ruby.py:65`, `conda.py:29`, `coursier.py:67`, `dart.py:27`, `dotnet.py:28`, `haskell.py:23`,
`lua.py:32`, `perl.py:23`, `swift.py:26`). `Var('PATH')` defaults to `''`, so when `PATH` is unset or empty the hook
runs with `PATH=<bin>:` (`<bin>;` on Windows). An empty `PATH` entry means "the current directory" to `execvp`, to
shells and to `parse_shebang.find_executable`; hooks run in the repository root, so any executable file committed to
the repository whose name matches a command the hook runs (`git`, `sh`, `python3`, …) would be executed. That turns
an untrusted repository into code execution for a user whose `PATH` happens to be empty.

snp builds these patches with `snp_core::env::EnvPatch::prepend_path(key, dirs)`, which renders
`d1 PATHSEP … dn PATHSEP $key` only when `$key` is set and non-empty, and `d1 PATHSEP … dn` otherwise. When `PATH` is
set and non-empty the result is byte-identical to pre-commit's, so no hook output changes; the divergence is only
the missing current-directory entry.

##### Examples

Patch `('PATH', ('/env/bin', os.pathsep, Var('PATH')))` applied to three environments (POSIX):

| startup `PATH` | pre-commit 4.6.2 hook `PATH` | snp hook `PATH` |
|---|---|---|
| unset | `/env/bin:` | `/env/bin` |
| `` (empty) | `/env/bin:` | `/env/bin` |
| `/usr/bin` | `/env/bin:/usr/bin` | `/env/bin:/usr/bin` |

End to end the difference cannot be observed through the CLI: with `PATH` unset or empty both tools fail before any
hook runs, because neither can find `git` (`find_executable` searches `PATH`, and git sets `PATH` itself before it
runs a hook script). The divergence protects library callers and every activation computed from an `Env` without
`PATH` (snp-lang's `ToolProbe`/`CmdRunner` paths, tests, embedders). It is pinned by the unit test
`prepend_path_without_trailing_separator` in `crates/snp-core/src/env.rs`; the scenario file records why no
differential scenario exists.

### D-SEC-08

TLS + sha256 verified before extraction; safe extraction

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| toolchain downloads (node, go, rustup, ruby helpers) are not verified | TLS + sha256 verified before extraction; safe extraction |

##### Rationale

pre-commit 4.6.2 trusts whatever bytes its toolchain bootstraps receive:

* **go** — `golang._install_go` (`golang.py:101-121`) streams `https://dl.google.com/go/go{version}.{os}-{arch}.{ext}`
  with `urllib.request.urlopen` and unpacks it with `tarfile.extractall`/`zipfile.extractall`, no checksum and no
  extraction filter (Python 3.12 still defaults to the `fully_trusted` filter: absolute names, `..`, links out of the
  tree and device files are honoured);
* **node** — `nodeenv --prebuilt` downloads the node archive (`nodeenv.py:811-865`) without checking `SHASUMS256.txt`;
* **rust** — `rust.install_rust_with_toolchain` (`rust.py:83-108`) downloads `https://sh.rustup.rs` and **executes**
  it;
* **ruby** — the vendored `rbenv`/`ruby-build`/`ruby-download` tarballs are unpacked with `tarfile.extractall`
  without a filter (`ruby.py:81-85`).

TLS protects the transport, not the content: a compromised mirror, a corporate TLS-intercepting proxy with a trusted
CA, a poisoned CDN edge or a tampered cache all deliver arbitrary executables that pre-commit then runs as the user,
and a hostile archive can write outside the environment directory. snp (ADR-034, ADR-077, ARCHITECTURE §6.3):

* downloads only over `https` (an `http://` archive mirror needs `SNP_ALLOW_INSECURE_MIRROR=1`, and even then the
  checksum manifest comes over TLS from the canonical origin or an explicit https `SNP_NODE_SHASUMS_URL` /
  `SNP_GO_JSON_URL`);
* verifies the sha256 of every archive **while streaming it into `<rand>.part`** and renames it to its final name only
  after the digest matched — against `SHASUMS256.txt` (node), the go.dev JSON (go), rustup's `.sha256` sidecar
  (rustup-init, a verified binary instead of a piped shell script) or a digest embedded in snp (uv, the ruby helpers);
* extracts in two passes into `<dest>.part-<rand>` (regular files and directories, then symlinks), refusing absolute,
  `..` and drive-prefixed names, device/FIFO/socket entries, hard links that do not point at a regular file extracted
  earlier, and symlinks that leave the tree or chain through another symlink (a `..` in a target must step back over
  a real directory of the tree, which also catches a chain spelled with a case variant on case-insensitive macOS and
  Windows filesystems: `X -> .` + `y -> x/..`); parents are opened without following links (Linux:
  `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS)`); setuid/setgid/sticky bits are stripped; metadata held in memory is
  bounded (1 MiB of tar records between two entries, so a gzip-bombed GNU long name fails as too large; 64 MiB of
  recorded names and link targets); the tree is renamed into place only when complete. Otherwise the result matches
  CPython `tarfile.extractall`: directories without an entry get `0o777 & ~umask`, a hard link's mode applies to the
  shared file.
* resolves node's `default`/`latest`/`lts` to the newest release of `index.json` that is not a pre-release and lists
  a build for the target (the unofficial builds' index for musl and riscv64). nodeenv 1.11.0 takes the first entry
  (only checking the x86_64-musl/riscv64 builds), which in October 2026 is `v27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0` — a pre-release
  everywhere and a 404 on x86_64 macOS (no `darwin-x64` build) — and has no arm64-musl case at all.

The divergence is invisible for genuine downloads: the same archives are installed at the same places. It only
appears when the bytes are not the published ones — then snp fails closed (exit 3, the message names the URL and
both digests) where pre-commit installs and runs them.

##### Examples

A go hook whose archive is replaced in transit (scenario `tests/differential/divergences/D-SEC-08.yaml`: a local
HTTPS interception proxy trusted through `SSL_CERT_FILE` serves the genuine go.dev JSON and a tampered
`go1.23.2.linux-amd64.tar.gz` whose `bin/go` prints `pwned`):

pre-commit 4.6.2 installs the tampered toolchain and the hook runs it (exit 1 here, because the fake `go install`
does not produce the hook binary; a real attacker's archive simply succeeds):

```
[INFO] Initializing environment for local.
[INFO] Installing environment for local.
[INFO] Once installed this environment will be reused.
[INFO] This may take a few minutes...
An unexpected error has occurred: CalledProcessError: command: ('/bin/sh', '<env>/.go/bin/go', 'install', './...')
return code: 1
stdout:
    pwned
stderr: (none)
Check the log at <store>/pre-commit.log
```

snp refuses the archive before anything is extracted (exit 3):

```
[INFO] Initializing environment for local.
[INFO] Installing environment for local.
[INFO] Once installed this environment will be reused.
[INFO] This may take a few minutes...
An unexpected error has occurred: NetError: checksum mismatch for https://dl.google.com/go/go1.23.2.linux-amd64.tar.gz: expected <go.dev sha256>, got <sha256 of the tampered archive>
Check the log at <store>/snp.log
```

Hermetic coverage of the snp side lives in `crates/snp-net/tests/net`: a tampered `http://` mirror archive is
rejected while the manifest still comes over TLS (`fetch::http_mirror_serves_only_bytes_the_tls_manifest_verifies`),
a checksum mismatch leaves no file at the final name, and the hostile-archive matrix (absolute, `..`, drive letters,
escaping and chained symlinks, hard links out of the tree, devices, FIFOs, setuid) is refused
(`archive::*`; fuzzed by `fuzz/fuzz_targets/net_archive_extract.rs`).

### D-SEC-09

Shebang lines are read at most 64 KiB deep; a longer first line counts as "no shebang".

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| shebang reads are unbounded | shebang line capped at 64 KiB (file-identify) |

##### Rationale

`parse_shebang.normalize_cmd` (`parse_shebang.py:65-85`) reads the shebang of every resolved hook executable with
identify's `parse_shebang`, which checks the first two bytes for `#!` and then calls `f.readline()` without a size
limit (`identify.py:178-219`). A hook script (or any executable found on `PATH`) whose first line is gigabytes long —
or a FIFO/device masquerading as one — makes pre-commit read it all into memory before running the hook. The same
reader classifies every extension-less executable file of the repository for `types` filtering, so a hostile file in
a pull request can exhaust memory on a reviewer's machine (ARCHITECTURE §11.4 "Shebang line: 64 KiB").

snp reads at most 64 KiB (file-identify's documented deviation, D-SEC-09 is its register entry); a longer first line is
treated as "no shebang", exactly like a first line that is not printable ASCII. No real interpreter line comes near
the bound — Linux itself executes at most 256 bytes of it (`BINPRM_BUF_SIZE`) — so the difference is observable only
with pathological files: pre-commit runs the interpreter named in the oversized line itself, snp lets the kernel
interpret the script (which truncates the line at 256 bytes). Exit statuses for every real-world script are unchanged.

##### Examples

`long.sh` (mode 755) = `#!/bin/echo ` + 70 000 × `a` + `\n`; a local hook `entry: ./long.sh`, `language: system`,
`pass_filenames: false`, `verbose: true`; `run --all-files` on Linux ≥ 5.1.

pre-commit 4.6.2 (verified with `pre_commit.xargs.xargs(('./long.sh',), ())` of the 4.6.2 oracle): `normalize_cmd`
returns `('/bin/echo', 'a'×70000, './long.sh')`; the hook output is 70 011 bytes: 70 000 × `a` + ` ./long.sh\n`.

snp: no shebang is parsed, `./long.sh` is spawned directly and the kernel runs `/bin/echo` with the first 256 bytes of
the line; the hook output is 254 bytes: 243 × `a` + ` ./long.sh\n`. Both runs end `Passed`, exit 0.

### D-SEC-10

Catastrophic regular expressions cannot hang snp: tier 1 is linear, tier 2 stops after 10⁸ backtracking steps with
an error.

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| catastrophic regexes hang (tier-1-able patterns are exponential in CPython; backtracking patterns unbounded) | linear tier 1; tier 2 `backtrack_limit` 1e8 → `An error has occurred: snp: regular expression {pattern!r} exceeded the backtracking limit on {path!r}` (exit 1) |

##### Rationale

pre-commit matches `files`, `exclude`, `types`-independent filters and pygrep entries with CPython's `re`
(`pre_commit/commands/run.py:60-70`, `pre_commit/languages/pygrep.py`), a backtracking engine without any step or
time limit. A pattern such as `^(.+/)*\.pre-commit-config\.yaml$` is exponential in the depth of a non-matching path
and `(?:(?=a)a+)+(?<!a)b` in the length of a run of `a`; a hostile `.pre-commit-config.yaml` in a pull request (or
a hostile file name meeting an innocent-looking pattern) makes `pre-commit run` spin for minutes or forever
(01 Addendum §A.6.13 D7, D8).

snp lowers every pattern it can to the `regex` crate (tier 1, 01 Addendum §A.6.9), which guarantees linear-time
matching: D8 patterns give CPython's answer without the exponential blow-up — no visible difference except time.
Patterns that need backtracking (look-around, back-references, conditionals, atomic groups, possessive repeats)
run on `fancy-regex` (tier 2) behind a mandatory linear prefilter (§A.6.11) and with `backtrack_limit` = 10⁸
(≈ 2.5 s on one core). Exceeding it is `MatchError::Backtrack`; for `files`/`exclude` it aborts the run with the
message above and exit 1 — never "not matched", which could silently skip a security hook (01 Addendum §A.10 Q6,
DECISIONS Appendix B). For pygrep the hook fails with the same message. Real configurations stay several orders of
magnitude below the limit (corpus frequency 0): a regex that takes 10⁸ steps on one file name is a bug or an attack.

##### Examples

A local hook `language: fail`, `entry: the files pattern matched`, `files: '(?:(?=a)a+)+(?<!a)b'`; the repository
holds the empty file `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab` (26 × `a` + `b`) and the config; `run --all-files`.

pre-commit 4.6.2 (CPython 3.12.3; bytes captured with the same `fail`/filter code of pre-commit 4.1.0 on 3.12.3):
`re.search` explores 2²⁵ partitions of the `a` run for ≈ 5.4 s, finds no match and prints, exit 0:

```text
matched..............................................(no files to check)Skipped
```

Each further `a` doubles the time (30 × `a`: ≈ 90 s; 40 × `a`: about a day).

snp: the relaxed prefilter `(?:a+)+b` matches, the backtracking engine hits the 10⁸-step limit after ≈ 2.5 s
(`MatchError::Backtrack`; from 26 × `a` on, independent of the length) and the run aborts, exit 1:

```text
An error has occurred: snp: regular expression '(?:(?=a)a+)+(?<!a)b' exceeded the backtracking limit on 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab'
```

The tier-1 half (D8, same answer, different time): `files: '^(.+/)*\.pre-commit-config\.yaml$'` with a file at
`d/d/…/d/x` (5 000 levels deep) never finishes in CPython; snp answers "not matched" in milliseconds
(`crates/snp-pyre/tests/backtrack.rs`). The 10⁸-step stop is tested by
`crates/snp-pyre/tests/perf.rs::perf_catastrophic_tier2_pattern_hits_the_backtrack_limit`.

### D-SEC-11

depth 512, 1 M constructed nodes, 16 MiB file limits → YAML error

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| YAML alias bombs / deep nesting / huge files exhaust memory or the stack | depth 512, 1 M constructed nodes, 16 MiB file limits → YAML error |

##### Rationale

PyYAML builds Python objects: an alias is a reference to the same object, so a "billion laughs" document of ten
levels of ten aliases costs nothing to *load* — but the value it returns holds 12,345,679,021 nodes when expanded,
and anything that walks it (validation, `repr`, a re-dump, a `cfgv::Value` tree) explodes. Nesting is limited only
by the C composer's stack and Python's recursion limit, and the file size not at all. snp materialises the loaded
document as a `cfgv::Value` tree and must never overflow a stack or exhaust memory on input it reads from a
repository it does not control (ARCHITECTURE §11.1, §11.4). It therefore enforces, as YAML errors of class
`YAMLError` that cfgv reports like any other load error:

* **16 MiB** of input (`Limits::max_bytes`), checked before parsing:
  `the input is N bytes long, more than the limit of 16777216 bytes`;
* **512 levels** of nesting (`Limits::max_depth`), counted while composing (an iterative composer: nesting costs heap,
  never stack) and again on the value after aliases and merges are expanded:
  `found a node nested deeper than the limit of 512 levels` with the mark of the first collection beyond it;
* **1,000,000 constructed nodes** (`Limits::max_constructed_nodes`), counting every node of the composed document
  (and, for `compose_all`, every document), and every use of an alias in the expanded value — computed on the shared
  node graph in linear time, before anything is copied: `found more than the limit of 1000000 nodes (aliases count at
  every use)` with the mark of the node whose copies cross the limit. The same budget is charged with the work of
  `<<` merge keys — one unit per merge key, per merged mapping flattened (also an empty one: `l: &L [{}, {}, …]`
  merged by thousands of mappings copies nothing but would take K × M steps) and per pair copied — and with the
  limb work of a sexagesimal `!!int "1:2:3:…"` (quadratic in CPython as well). Hex, octal and binary integers, which
  CPython parses without a digit limit, are parsed in linear time;
* a value that contains itself (`&a [*a]`, `&a {x: *a}`), which a tree cannot hold, is PyYAML's own constructor
  error for unconstructable recursion: `found unconstructable recursive node` at the recursive node.

The deviation is safe: real configurations are far inside every limit (the largest of the 10 §7.4.6 corpus has a few
hundred nodes and a nesting depth under 10), every limit is reported as an ordinary `InvalidConfigError` (exit 1)
instead of a hang, an out-of-memory kill or a stack overflow, and no document within the limits is affected — the
differential corpus of `crates/snp-yaml/tests/vectors` loads byte-identically. The 10 × 10 bomb is rejected in well
under 100 ms with a peak heap far below 64 MB (`crates/snp-yaml/tests/{perf,memory}.rs`); a 10,000-deep document is a
clean error on a 256 KiB thread stack (`tests/acceptance.rs`).

##### Examples

The scenario `tests/differential/divergences/D-SEC-11.yaml` validates three configurations whose unknown key `x`
holds the hostile value (pre-commit never descends into an unknown key, so it only warns).

`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, an alias bomb:

```yaml
repos: []
x:
  a0: &a0 [lol, lol, lol, lol, lol, lol, lol, lol, lol, lol]
  a1: &a1 [*a0, *a0, *a0, *a0, *a0, *a0, *a0, *a0, *a0, *a0]
  # … a2 to a8 alike …
  a9: &a9 [*a8, *a8, *a8, *a8, *a8, *a8, *a8, *a8, *a8, *a8]
```

`pre-commit validate-config .pre-commit-config.yaml` (4.6.2): exit 0, stdout

```
[WARNING] Unexpected key(s) present at root: x
```

snp: exit 1, stdout

```

==> File .pre-commit-config.yaml
=====> found more than the limit of 1000000 nodes (aliases count at every use)
  in "<unicode string>", line 3, column 7
```

`deep.yaml` = `repos: []` and `x: ` followed by 600 `[` and 600 `]`: pre-commit exits 0 with the same warning; snp
exits 1 with `=====> found a node nested deeper than the limit of 512 levels` and
`  in "<unicode string>", line 2, column 515`.

`recursive.yaml` = `repos: []` and `x: &a [*a]`: pre-commit exits 0 with the same warning (the value is a list that
contains itself); snp exits 1 with `=====> found unconstructable recursive node` and
`  in "<unicode string>", line 2, column 4`.

### D-SEC-12

more than 64 MiB fails closed before the legacy hook and the hooks run: An error has occurred: FatalError: snp: hook stdin exceeds 64 MiB; refusing to run…

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| pre-push stdin (and the `use_stdin` copy) is read without a limit | more than 64 MiB fails closed before the legacy hook and the hooks run: `An error has occurred: FatalError: snp: hook stdin exceeds 64 MiB; refusing to run hooks on a truncated ref list` (exit 1); never truncated |

*The rationale and examples of this divergence are not written yet; the register entry above is
normative.*

### D-SEC-13

as root (euid 0), a store owned by a non-root uid is refused unless `SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1`

* **Class:** SEC (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.3)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| a store writable by another user is used as is, including when running as root (tools and environments that user can replace get executed) | as root (euid 0), a store owned by a non-root uid is refused with `An error has occurred: FatalError: snp refuses to run as root from a store owned by uid <n>: <path>; set SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1 to trust it` (exit 1) unless `SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1`; other foreign owners only warn (D-DIAG-05) |

##### Rationale

pre-commit uses whatever directory `PRE_COMMIT_HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME`/`~/.cache` names and executes the hook
repositories and environments it finds there. When root runs pre-commit against a store that an unprivileged user
owns (a CI cache volume mounted into a container, `sudo` with a preserved `HOME`), that user can replace any
interpreter, `node_modules` entry or clone in the store and gets code execution as root — git refuses the analogous
repository situation since 2.35.2 (`safe.directory`).

snp's `Store::ensure_created` checks the store's owner (ADR-044, ADR-077): owned by the effective uid → used; owned by
another uid → used with one stderr warning (D-DIAG-05), which keeps volume-mounted CI caches working; but when the
effective uid is 0 and the owner is not root, the store is refused with the FatalError above (exit 1) unless
`SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1` is set, in which case it is used with the warning. A world-writable store without the
sticky bit is refused for every user (symlink planting).

Safe: the refusal happens before anything from the store is executed, names the escape hatch, and affects only the
root-over-user case where the trust boundary is crossed.

##### Examples

Needs root and a store owned by another uid, which the differential harness cannot arrange portably; the scenario
records `status: unit`. `crates/snp-store/tests/support/behaviour.rs::foreign_store_as_root_is_refused_unless_allowed`
(posix, runs in the CI container as root) chowns a store to uid 1000 and expects, exit 1:

```text
An error has occurred: FatalError: snp refuses to run as root from a store owned by uid 1000: <store>; set SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1 to trust it
```

and, re-run with `SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1`, success with the stderr warning
`[WARNING] the snp store <store> is owned by uid 1000, not by the current user`. pre-commit 4.6.2 uses such a store
without a word.

## 5.4 STORE and BRAND — forced by FD-2 and FD-1

### D-STORE-01

own store `SNP_HOME` > `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/snp` > `~/.cache/snp`, versioned layout, no SQLite; refuses pre-commit's store; crash log named by brand

* **Class:** STORE (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| store `$PRE_COMMIT_HOME` or `~/.cache/pre-commit` (SQLite `db.db`); crash log `pre-commit.log` there | own store `SNP_HOME` > `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/snp` > `~/.cache/snp` (Windows `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\snp`), versioned layout, no SQLite; refuses pre-commit's store; crash log named by brand in snp's store; the crash-log body (below the version block) is snp's |

##### Rationale

Owner decision FD-2 (ADR-011, ADR-024): snp keeps its own store. Sharing pre-commit's would mix two layouts and two
lock protocols in one directory (pre-commit locks with `msvcrt` byte ranges on Windows, snp with `LockFileEx`), make
`snp clean` delete pre-commit's `db.db`, and let either tool's environments break the other's health checks.

`snp_store::resolve_location`: `SNP_HOME` (non-empty), else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/snp` (non-empty, every OS, as pre-commit
honours it), else `expanduser("~/.cache")/snp` — `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\snp` on Windows, `~/.cache/snp` on macOS,
pre-commit's own default shape (14 P-65); relative values resolve against the invocation cwd and the result is
`realpath`'d like pre-commit's. `PRE_COMMIT_HOME` is read only to compute pre-commit's store and refuse it: a resolved
path equal to it, or a directory whose README starts with pre-commit's signature, is a FatalError (`snp refuses to
use pre-commit's cache directory <path>; set SNP_HOME to another directory`, M7). The layout is versioned
(`repos-v1`, `keys-v1`, `configs-v1`, `tools-v1`, `cache-v1`, ARCHITECTURE §5.2) and has no database. The crash log
is `<store>/pre-commit.log` in the compat brand and `<store>/snp.log` in the snp brand (ADR-013).

Safe: everything observable stays pre-commit's except store-derived paths (`Check the log at …`, `Stashing unstaged
files to …`), which the comparison tiers treat as Tier C. CI cache recipes must cache `~/.cache/snp` (user docs).

##### Examples

Recorded with pre-commit 4.6.2 on CPython 3.12.3 (a venv built from the hash lock `xtask/oracle/requirements-pc462.txt`); `<W>` is the scratch root, `<store>` the store directory.

An invalid config (`repos: 1`), `run --all-files` with `HOME=<W>/home`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` unset
(`tests/differential/divergences/D-STORE-01.yaml`).

pre-commit 4.6.2 with `PRE_COMMIT_HOME=<W>/pch`, exit 1:

```text
An error has occurred: InvalidConfigError:
==> File .pre-commit-config.yaml
==> At Config()
==> At key: repos
=====> Expected array but got 'int'
Check the log at <W>/pch/pre-commit.log
```

(and `<W>/pch` now holds `README`, `db.db`, `.lock`, `pre-commit.log`). snp prints the same lines except the last:
`Check the log at <W>/home/.cache/snp/pre-commit.log` (compat brand) / `…/snp/snp.log` (snp brand); `<W>/pch` is
neither created nor read. With `XDG_CACHE_HOME=<W>/xdg` pre-commit logs to `<W>/xdg/pre-commit/pre-commit.log` and
snp to `<W>/xdg/snp/pre-commit.log`.

Unit coverage: `crates/snp-store/tests/catalog.rs::t10_sto_01_default_directory_precedence`,
`support/behaviour.rs::location_matrix`, `m7_refuses_pre_commit_store_by_path_and_by_readme`.

### D-STORE-02

snp never touches pre-commit's directories; clean always prints Cleaned {snp store}.

* **Class:** STORE (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| `clean` also removes `~/.pre-commit`; `gc`/`clean` operate on pre-commit's store | snp never touches pre-commit's directories; `clean` always prints `Cleaned {snp store}.` |

*The rationale and examples of this divergence are not written yet; the register entry above is
normative.*

### D-DATA-04

gc removes *restored* patches older than 30 days (never unrestored ones) — class STORE

* **Class:** STORE (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| restored stash patches are kept forever | gc removes *restored* patches older than 30 days (never unrestored ones) — class STORE |

##### Rationale

pre-commit writes the unstaged changes of every stashing run to `<store>/patch<epoch>-<pid>`
(`staged_files_only.py:68`) and never deletes them, not even in `gc` (03 §7.10): long-lived stores accumulate one
file per commit with unstaged changes, each possibly holding secrets the user never committed.

snp's stash (WP-23) writes its patches to `<store>/patches/` and a journal `run-<pid>-<rand>.snp-journal` that names
the patch; the journal is deleted when the restore completes. `Store::sweep` (run by gc under the exclusive store
lock) removes a `patch*` file only when it is older than 30 days **and** no remaining journal mentions it (a whole
file-name match) by a journal that is not in state `restored`/`done` (a journal left behind by a crash between the
restore and its deletion protects nothing: that patch's content is back in the worktree). A patch whose restore failed
or was interrupted — the user's only copy of their work — keeps its journal and is never removed; journals are never
removed by gc.

`clean` (pre-commit: `rmtree` of the whole store, `commands/clean.py:10-16`) removes snp's own layout and likewise
keeps recovery data, so a differential `tree` comparison of `clean` differs in these entries, all of them deliberate:

* every journal, the patches of unrestored journals, and every `patch*` younger than an hour — a run stashing in
  another worktree creates its patch before it journals it (ARCHITECTURE §4 steps 5–6) and takes the shared store lock
  only at its first repository use, so such a patch may be about to be restored; the journals are re-read right before
  each removal;
* `.lock`, so that processes already waiting on the global lock keep excluding each other (removing it would let a
  waiter and a newcomer lock two different inodes);
* files outside snp's layout (anything a user put into `SNP_HOME`), and snp 1.x names unless the README carries the
  1.x signature: snp deletes only what it can prove it created.

Safe: only patches whose content is already back in the worktree are deleted, and only after a month in which the
`[INFO] Restored changes from <patch>.` line pointed at them.

##### Examples

Not reproducible through the CLI within a test run (the patch must be 30 days old); the behaviour is pinned by
`crates/snp-store/tests/support/behaviour.rs::sweep_keeps_unrestored_patches_and_referenced_tools`, which calls
`Store::sweep` with a clock 31 days ahead: `patch1700000000-41` (no journal) is removed, `patch1700000000-42`
(mentioned by `run-42-abcd.snp-journal`, state `failed`) and the journal stay, and `patch1700000000-43` (mentioned by
the `restored` journal `run-43-abcd.snp-journal`) is removed. `clean_retires_the_layout_but_keeps_unknown_and_recovery_data`
pins the `clean` entries above. pre-commit 4.6.2 keeps both patches
(`gc` prints `0 repo(s) removed.` and never looks at them); the scenario file records `status: unit`.

### D-BRAND-01

snp brand: snp 2.0.0, the §3.3 substitutions and argparse texts rendered with prog snp; compat brand: byte-identical

* **Class:** BRAND (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.4)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| `--version` and texts | snp brand: `snp 2.0.0`, the §3.3 substitutions and argparse texts rendered with prog `snp`; compat brand: byte-identical |

##### Rationale

FD-1 fixes the product identity: invoked under any name but `pre-commit`, the tool is snp and says so. Under the
`pre-commit` name (a symlink, hard link or copy; COMPATIBILITY §3.1) every byte stays pre-commit 4.6.2's, so scripts,
CI greps and `pre-commit --version` parsers keep working (ADR-023).

In the snp brand the argparse texts are **rendered**, not substituted (ADR-058): argparse wraps usage, help and usage
errors relative to `usage: {prog} {cmd} `, so the 7-character-shorter prog `snp` moves wrap points and continuation
indents (`init-templatedir`: 35 → 28 columns). `snp_argparse` renders them from `SNP_SPEC` with prog `snp`; the goldens
(`crates/snp-cli/tests/goldens/snp.json`, `cargo xtask cli-goldens`) are produced by a real CPython 3.13.14 argparse
built from `export_json(SNP_SPEC, "snp")` and, for every parser identical to pre-commit's, cross-checked against the
prog-patched oracle `target/oracle/pc462-py313/bin/pre-commit-snp-prog`. The help strings of `main.py` that name the
tool (`main.py:222, 245, 273, 290, 299, 335`) read `snp` in the snp brand (COMPATIBILITY §3.3).

`--version` is the one argparse text that is not a pure prog substitution: `%(prog)s 4.6.2` would print `snp 4.6.2`,
which names a version of snp that does not exist; the snp brand's version action is `%(prog)s 2.0.0`.

Why it is safe: the divergence is confined to the snp brand, which pre-commit users only reach by typing `snp`; the
compat brand reproduces pre-commit 4.6.2 byte for byte (`crates/snp-cli/tests/goldens/compat.json`, 490 cases at
the 12 §A.16 width matrix, all generated from pre-commit 4.6.2 on CPython 3.13.14). Exit codes and streams are the
same in both brands.

##### Examples

`--version` (stdout, exit 0):

```text
$ pre-commit --version          # pre-commit 4.6.2, and snp through a `pre-commit` link
pre-commit 4.6.2
$ snp --version
snp 2.0.0
```

`init-templatedir -h` (first lines; the continuation indent follows the prog):

```text
$ pre-commit init-templatedir -h
usage: pre-commit init-templatedir [-h] [--color {auto,always,never}]
                                   [-c CONFIG] [--no-allow-missing-config]
$ snp init-templatedir -h
usage: snp init-templatedir [-h] [--color {auto,always,never}] [-c CONFIG]
                            [--no-allow-missing-config]
```

Usage errors name the prog of the reporting parser:

```text
$ pre-commit sample-config --color bogus
usage: pre-commit sample-config [-h] [--color {auto,always,never}]
pre-commit sample-config: error: argument --color: invalid use_color value: 'bogus'
$ snp sample-config --color bogus
usage: snp sample-config [-h] [--color {auto,always,never}]
snp sample-config: error: argument --color: invalid use_color value: 'bogus'
```

Help strings that name the tool (`snp -h`, commands block):

```text
    clean               Clean out snp files.
    install             Install the snp script.
```

The scenario `tests/differential/divergences/D-BRAND-01.yaml` runs these commands in the snp brand against the
unpatched oracle, where they must keep differing.

## 5.5 PLAT — platform

### D-PLAT-02

Windows: a missing absolute shebang interpreter (`#!/bin/sh`) falls back to the interpreter's basename on `PATH`.

* **Class:** PLAT (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)
* **Tests:** `d_plat_02_basename_fallback` (`crates/snp-proc/src/resolve.rs`, the Windows rule exercised on every OS).

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Windows: a missing absolute shebang interpreter (`#!/bin/sh`) fails the hook / crashes the legacy hook | falls back to the interpreter's basename on PATH (Git for Windows semantics) |

##### Rationale

`normalize_cmd` interprets one level of shebang on every platform (`parse_shebang.py:65-85`). On Windows the
interpreter of `#!/bin/sh` or `#!/bin/bash` is the path `/bin/sh`, which `normexe` treats as a path
(`os.altsep` is `/`): `isfile('\bin\sh')` on the current drive is false, so pre-commit reports
``Executable `/bin/sh` not found`` and fails the hook (rc 1); a legacy hook with such a shebang crashes `hook-impl`
with `An unexpected error has occurred: ExecutableNotFoundError: …` (exit 3, 14 P-22/P-23). Git for Windows runs the
very same scripts by looking up the interpreter's basename on `PATH` (`compat/mingw.c:1898-1910`), and inside
`git commit` its `usr\bin` (with `sh.exe` and `bash.exe`) is on `PATH`.

snp applies Git for Windows' rule, only where pre-commit would fail: when the interpreter came from a shebang (never
for an explicit `entry:` path), starts with `/`, and is not a file, `find_executable(basename)` is tried; if that also
fails, pre-commit's message (naming the original interpreter) is kept. Every script that works under pre-commit
resolves exactly as before; scripts that fail under pre-commit now run the way `git` itself runs them. POSIX is
unaffected (the fallback is compiled in but disabled).

##### Examples

Windows, Git for Windows on `PATH` (`C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` provides `sh.exe`), a local hook
`entry: ./hook.sh`, `language: script`, where `hook.sh` is `#!/bin/sh` + `echo ran`; `run --all-files`:

pre-commit 4.6.2 (exit 1):

```
script hook..............................................................Failed
- hook id: script-hook
- exit code: 1

Executable `/bin/sh` not found
```

snp (exit 0): `script hook…Passed` — `sh.exe` runs `./hook.sh`.

### D-PLAT-03

Windows: batch-file (`.cmd`/`.bat`) hooks receive their arguments literally (BatBadBut-safe quoting); an argument
containing a line break fails the hook with a clear message.

* **Class:** PLAT, security relevant (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)
* **Tests:** `batch_line_break_refusal` (`crates/snp-proc/src/spawn.rs`), the message golden in
  `crates/snp-proc/src/messages.rs`.

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Windows: batch-file (`.cmd`/`.bat`) arguments with `&`, `^`, `%VAR%` are interpreted by cmd.exe | Rust's BatBadBut-safe quoting; arguments containing CR/LF fail the hook with ``Executable `{cmd0}` cannot receive an argument containing a line break: {repr}`` (rc 1) — class SEC |

##### Rationale

A `.cmd`/`.bat` hook (npm shims such as `prettier.CMD` are batch files) is started by `CreateProcess`, which hands the
command line to `cmd.exe /c`. CPython builds that line with `subprocess.list2cmdline`, which quotes only arguments
containing a space or tab: a file name like `a&calc.txt`, `x|y.md` or `%PATH%.txt` reaches cmd.exe unquoted and is
*executed* or expanded (CVE-2024-24576 class, "BatBadBut"; 14 A.1 #6, P-25/P-26). File names come from the
repository, so this is command injection driven by repository content.

snp spawns through Rust's `std::process::Command`, which since 1.77.2 quotes every batch argument for cmd.exe
(`"a&calc.txt"`, `%` rewritten to `%%cd:~,%`), so the hook receives exactly the file names git reported. The one input
cmd.exe cannot receive safely is an argument containing CR or LF; Rust refuses it with an opaque
`batch file arguments are invalid`. snp checks for it before spawning and fails that partition like any spawn error
(rc 1, output = the message + `\n`):

``Executable `C:\…\run.cmd` cannot receive an argument containing a line break: 'a\nb'``

The quoting changes the command line only for arguments that pre-commit would let cmd.exe interpret; ordinary
arguments are passed unchanged. The longer quoted lines are kept under cmd.exe's limit by D-PLAT-09.

##### Examples

Windows, a local hook `entry: run.cmd` (`@echo %*`), `language: system`, run on a tracked file `a&echo INJECTED.txt`:

pre-commit 4.6.2: cmd.exe runs `run.cmd a` and then `echo INJECTED.txt`; the output contains `INJECTED.txt` on a line
of its own.

snp: the batch file receives the single argument `"a&echo INJECTED.txt"` and echoes it verbatim.

With `args: ["line1\nline2"]` pre-commit's line is cut at the line feed by cmd.exe; snp fails the hook with
``Executable `run.cmd` cannot receive an argument containing a line break: 'line1\nline2'`` (`- exit code: 1`).

absolute path kept

* **Class:** PLAT (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Windows: config/`--files` on another drive → `ValueError` (relpath) exit 3 | absolute path kept |

### D-PLAT-08

clear error, exit 1

* **Class:** PLAT (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| cygwin/MSYS2 git on Windows: a warning, then undefined behaviour | clear error, exit 1 |

##### Rationale

A Cygwin or MSYS2 build of git speaks POSIX paths (`/cygdrive/c/…`, `/c/…`) and resolves them through its emulation
DLL; a native Windows program cannot use what it prints (`rev-parse` roots, `--git-path index`, `ls-files` paths) and
git cannot use the native paths it is given. pre-commit's guard (`git.check_for_cygwin_mismatch`, `git.py:210-230`)
only compares `get_root()` with `/`, which on native Windows Python is never true (`ntpath.abspath` always yields a
drive path, 14 #13): it is dead code, and the run continues with mismatched paths — wrong file lists, a stash that
cannot be restored, crashes deep in the run (undefined behaviour with the user's unstaged work at stake).

snp detects such a git before any repository call: on Windows, the directory of the resolved `git.exe` holds the
emulation DLL (`cygwin1.dll`, `msys-2.0.dll`); Git for Windows' `cmd\`, `bin\` and `mingw64\bin\` launchers never
do. `version_gate` then stops with a `FatalError` (exit 1) naming the git it found and the fix. Elsewhere nothing
changes (the check is compiled out of the decision on Unix).

##### Examples

Windows, `PATH` starting with `C:\msys64\usr\bin` (MSYS2's `git.exe` next to `msys-2.0.dll`), `pre-commit run`
through the compat alias.

pre-commit 4.6.2 (native Windows Python): no warning (dead check), then undefined behaviour — typically
`An unexpected error has occurred: …` once a POSIX path from git meets a Windows path API, or a silent mis-selection
of files.

snp, exit **1**, stdout:

```
An error has occurred: FatalError: pre-commit does not support a Cygwin or MSYS2 git on Windows (found C:\msys64\usr\bin\git.exe); install Git for Windows (https://gitforwindows.org/) and put it first on PATH.
Check the log at <store>\pre-commit.log
```

(snp brand: `snp does not support …`.)

Regression tests: the detection (`exe::tests::cygwin_detection`, every OS: the DLL next to the executable decides)
and the brand texts (`messages::tests::cygwin_both_brands`). The scenario runs on the Windows CI runner with MSYS2.

### D-PLAT-09

Windows: partitions of a `.cmd`/`.bat` hook are re-split when the real (quoted) command line would exceed cmd.exe's
8191-character limit.

* **Class:** PLAT (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)
* **Tests:** `d_plat_09_batch_partitions_are_resplit`, `batch_argument_lengths_follow_rusts_quoting`
  (`crates/snp-proc/src/xargs.rs`).

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Windows: `.cmd` partitions can exceed 8191 characters after quoting (crash) | partitions re-split |

##### Rationale

For a batch-file hook `xargs.xargs` budgets `8192 - len(cmd.exe) - len(' /c ') - 1024` characters (`xargs.py:155-164`)
and partitions by the *unquoted* length of each argument plus one separator. The command line cmd.exe finally
receives is longer: arguments that need quoting gain two quotes, embedded quotes are doubled, and with D-PLAT-03 every
`%` becomes the 8-character `%%cd:~,%`. File names with many such characters push a partition past cmd.exe's hard
limit of 8191 characters, and the hook fails with `The command line is too long.` (or `[WinError 206]` from
`CreateProcess` above 32 767), which pre-commit reports as a failed hook or a crash.

snp computes partitions exactly as pre-commit does (`partition` is an exact port, so partition boundaries and the
order of output never change for ordinary names), then measures each partition's real Rust batch command line
(`cmd.exe /e:ON /v:OFF /d /c ""<script>" <quoted args…>"`, UTF-16 units) and halves any partition that would exceed
8191 characters until it fits. Files keep their order; only the number of hook invocations grows, and only for
partitions that could not have run at all.

##### Examples

Windows, a local hook `entry: check.cmd` (`@exit /b 0`), `language: system`, `require_serial: true`, and 1 000
tracked files named `a b0000` … `a b0999` (7 characters, one space each).

pre-commit 4.6.2: the unquoted budget (~7 100 characters with `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe`) admits ~887 names
per partition at 8 characters each; `list2cmdline` quotes every name (10 characters each), so cmd.exe receives
~8 900 characters and the hook fails with `The command line is too long.` (`- exit code: 1`).

snp: the same partitions are computed, then each one whose quoted line exceeds 8 191 characters is halved; every
invocation fits and the hook passes (exit 0).

### D-PLAT-10

Windows: the CPU count is `available_parallelism` (`GetSystemInfo`), not `GetActiveProcessorCount(ALL_PROCESSOR_GROUPS)`;
macOS and Windows: `PYTHON_CPU_COUNT` is ignored, while pre-commit on CPython ≥ 3.13 honours it there.

* **Class:** PLAT (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)
