  `t10_xrg_01_cpu_count_is_the_affinity_count` (`crates/snp-proc/tests/catalog.rs`); `PYTHON_CPU_COUNT`: 14 §A.6
  W18, checked on the macOS and Windows runners by `cargo xtask platform-facts` (PF-11 records that CPython 3.13
  honours the variable there, PF-22 that snp does not; PF-22 needs `snp __debug platform`, until then it is reported
  as unverified).

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Windows CPU count = `GetActiveProcessorCount(ALL_PROCESSOR_GROUPS)`; on macOS and Windows under CPython ≥ 3.13 a positive `PYTHON_CPU_COUNT` replaces the count (`multiprocessing.cpu_count()`; Linux uses `sched_getaffinity`, which ignores it) | `available_parallelism` (differs only above 64 logical CPUs; no `unsafe`); `PYTHON_CPU_COUNT` ignored on every OS (14 A.9 Q3; `SNP_JOBS` sets the count) |

##### Rationale

`xargs.cpu_count()` falls back to `multiprocessing.cpu_count()` on Windows (no `sched_getaffinity`), which CPython
implements with `GetActiveProcessorCount(ALL_PROCESSOR_GROUPS)`: every logical CPU of every processor group
(`posixmodule.c:14448-14451`, 14 A.1 #14). The count sets `target_concurrency`, which decides `max_args` and thus the
partition boundaries of every non-serial hook (`xargs.py:76-117`).

Calling `GetActiveProcessorCount` needs FFI, and snp forbids `unsafe` in all of its crates (FD-5, ARCHITECTURE §11.6;
the `snp-sys` crate proposed in 14 A.7.1 was rejected). Rust's `std::thread::available_parallelism` reports the
processors of the current processor group, and Windows puts at most 64 logical CPUs in a group, so the two counts are
identical on every machine with at most 64 logical CPUs — every desktop, laptop and standard CI runner. Above 64 the
count may be lower in snp, giving fewer, larger partitions: the same files are checked, in the same shuffled order,
with the same exit status; only the number of hook invocations (visible to hooks that print per invocation) differs.
`PRE_COMMIT_NO_CONCURRENCY`, `TRAVIS` and `require_serial` behave identically on both sides. On Linux both tools count
the affinity mask (`sched_getaffinity`), on macOS both use `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`.

`PYTHON_CPU_COUNT` (CPython 3.13+, like `-X cpu_count`): `os.cpu_count()` returns the variable's value when it is
a positive integer. pre-commit reaches `os.cpu_count()` only through the `multiprocessing.cpu_count()` fallback, so on
Linux (`sched_getaffinity` first) it ignores the variable, as snp does; on macOS and Windows, under CPython 3.13 or
later, it uses it. snp ignores it everywhere (14 A.9 Q3): it is a Python-specific variable whose only effect is the
partitioning described above (the number of invocations, never the set of files checked or the exit status), and
`SNP_JOBS` is snp's own knob. Under CPython 3.12 the two tools agree on every OS.

##### Examples

Windows with 128 logical CPUs in two processor groups, a hook `entry: snp-probe count` over 2 000 files.

pre-commit 4.6.2: `target_concurrency()` = 128, `max_args` = max(4, ⌈2000/128⌉) = 16 → 125 invocations, 125 output
lines `16`.

snp: `cpu_count()` = 64 (the current group), `max_args` = ⌈2000/64⌉ = 32 → 63 invocations (62 × `32`, 1 × `16`).

Both exit 0 and check all 2 000 files.

macOS with 10 CPUs, `PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=3`, pre-commit 4.6.2 on CPython 3.13, the same hook over 2 000 files.

pre-commit 4.6.2: `target_concurrency()` = 3, `max_args` = ⌈2000/3⌉ = 667 → 3 invocations (667, 667, 666).

snp: `cpu_count()` = 10, `max_args` = 200 → 10 invocations of 200 files.

Both exit 0 and check all 2 000 files; under CPython 3.12, or on Linux, pre-commit makes the same 10 invocations.

### D-PLAT-12

tagged symlink (reading the reparse tag needs unsafe)

* **Class:** PLAT (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.5)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Windows: a directory junction is tagged `directory` | tagged `symlink` (reading the reparse tag needs `unsafe`) |

##### Rationale

On Windows, CPython's `os.lstat` reports `S_IFLNK` only for `IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK`; a directory junction
(`IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT`) is a directory, so identify tags it `directory` (14 P-69). Rust's
`symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()` is true for every name-surrogate reparse point, junctions included, and
the reparse tag that tells them apart is reachable only through `FindFirstFileW`/`GetFileInformationByHandleEx` FFI
(`unsafe`, excluded by FD-5) or the unstable `windows_by_handle`. snp (file-identify's `FileKind::from_file_type`)
therefore tags a junction `symlink`.

Safe and narrow: git never lists a junction as a file (it stores symlinks, and junctions are created by tools outside
git), so the difference is reachable only through `--files`/stdin lists naming a junction; such a path is not a
regular file under either classification, so the default `types: [file]` excludes it in both tools.

##### Examples

Windows only. A junction `j` (`mklink /J j subdir`) passed with `run --files j` to two hooks, `types: [directory]` and
`types: [symlink]` (`tests/differential/divergences/D-PLAT-12.yaml`): pre-commit 4.6.2 passes `j` to the
`directory` hook and skips the `symlink` hook (`(no files to check)`); snp does the opposite. Both skip it for a
default `types: [file]` hook. Recorded on a Windows runner by WP-35's harness (no Windows oracle on the development
machine).

## 5.6 PERF — forced by FD-7/FD-8, invisible in hook output

### D-PERF-01

uv (`--seed`) with pip-config translation and a pip fallback; seeded packages may differ in version, and uv's resolver
can differ on pre-releases, yanked versions and extra-index strategy (FD-7); `SNP_PYTHON_INSTALLER=pip` restores pip's
resolver per env (ADR-073)

* **Class:** PERF (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| Python envs built with virtualenv + pip | uv (`--seed`) with pip-config translation and a pip fallback; seeded packages may differ in version, and uv's resolver can differ on pre-releases, yanked versions and extra-index strategy (FD-7); `SNP_PYTHON_INSTALLER=pip` restores pip's resolver per env (ADR-073) |

##### Rationale

pre-commit builds every `language: python` environment with `<its interpreter> -mvirtualenv <env> [-p X]` (cwd `/`)
and `python -mpip install . *deps` in the hook clone (`python.py:214-228`). That costs ≈ 0.25–0.4 s per venv and
seconds per install (04a §2.3, §11.1), and it needs a Python with virtualenv — which snp, a single binary, does not
have. snp (ADR-033, ADR-073, ARCHITECTURE §6.2) builds the environment with uv by default:

```
uv venv <env> --python <abs interp> --seed --no-project --no-config --no-python-downloads        (cwd /)
uv pip install --python <env>/bin/python --no-config [translated pip config] [.] *deps          (cwd = the clone)
```

* **Same interpreter choice.** `<abs interp>` is chosen by pre-commit's rules relative to a reference interpreter
  (`python3`, then `python`; Windows `py -3`, `python`): `default` and versions matching it use it, then the `py`
  launcher (Windows), `PATH`, `expanduser(version)`, and only then uv's discovery; env directory names are pre-commit's
  (`py_env-python3.12`).
* **Same environment shape.** `--seed` installs pip (and, below 3.12, setuptools and wheel), as virtualenv does, so
  hooks that shell out to `pip` keep working; the activation (`PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK`, `PYTHONHOME` unset,
  `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PATH`) is pre-commit's byte for byte (recorded goldens in `crates/snp-lang/testdata/group1/golden`).
* **Same configuration.** uv ignores `pip.conf` and `PIP_*`; snp reads them the way pip layers them and translates
  every setting that has an equivalent (index URLs with `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match`, find-links, trusted
  hosts, certificates, proxy, pre-releases, constraints, the inverted `no-build-isolation`, binary policies, timeout,
  keyring, hashes). `--no-config` keeps the hook repository's `uv.toml`/`[tool.uv]` from redirecting indexes. The
  `UV_*` variables that would change the interpreter, project or resolution are stripped; network, cache and TLS ones
  are kept; the uv cache is isolated (`cache-v1/uv`) unless `UV_CACHE_DIR` is set.
* **Fallback.** A pip setting without a translation, an `additional_dependencies` item that is a pip option uv rejects
  (`--user`, `--progress-bar=…`, `--use-pep517`, …), or no obtainable uv (no `$SNP_UV`, none next to snp, none ≥ 0.8.0
  on `PATH`, the pinned release cannot be downloaded) builds that environment with pip instead
  (`<interp> -m venv <env>` + pre-commit's `python -mpip install . *deps`). `SNP_PYTHON_INSTALLER=pip` forces pip for
  every environment, `=uv` forces uv and fails instead of falling back; the choice is recorded in the install state,
  and a different choice rebuilds the environment.

What remains different is what uv and pip themselves do differently: the seeded pip/setuptools versions (uv's
bundled seed versus virtualenv's embedded wheels), `pyvenv.cfg` (`uv = …`/`version_info = 3.12.3` versus
`virtualenv = …`/`version_info = 3.12.3.final.0`; snp's health check accepts both, 04a G5), and uv's resolver, which
can pick a different version than pip for pre-releases, yanked releases or multiple indexes (FD-7). Users who depend
on pip's resolution set `SNP_PYTHON_INSTALLER=pip`.

##### Examples

A local python hook with a dependency that prints which tool created its environment
(`tests/differential/divergences/D-PERF-01.yaml`; needs the network for `six`):

pre-commit 4.6.2, exit 0:

```
[INFO] Initializing environment for local:six.
[INFO] Installing environment for local.
[INFO] Once installed this environment will be reused.
[INFO] This may take a few minutes...
creator..................................................................Passed
- hook id: creator
- duration: 0.02s

virtualenv
```

snp, exit 0:

```
[INFO] Initializing environment for local:six.
[INFO] Installing environment for local.
[INFO] Once installed this environment will be reused.
[INFO] This may take a few minutes...
creator..................................................................Passed
- hook id: creator
- duration: 0.02s

uv
```

With `SNP_PYTHON_INSTALLER=pip`, snp prints `venv` (the standard library's creator writes neither key).

### D-PERF-02

placeholder install skipped

* **Class:** PERF (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| local `language: python` hooks without deps `pip install` a placeholder package | placeholder install skipped |

##### Rationale

A `repo: local` hook's prefix is the store's local-template directory (03 §7.7): the 4.6.2 `empty_template_*` files
for every language, `setup.py` among them (`setup(name='pre-commit-placeholder-package', version='0.0.0',
py_modules=[])`). pre-commit's python install always runs `python -mpip install . *deps` in the prefix
(`python.py:214-228`), so a local python hook **without** dependencies installs that empty placeholder package — a
setuptools build in an isolated build environment (downloading setuptools when it is not cached) for nothing: the
package has no modules, no entry points and no dependencies.

The step is also fragile: every language builds in the same shared local prefix, and before 4.5.1 a `target/` left by
a local rust hook made `pip install .` fail with `Multiple top-level packages discovered in a flat-layout` (04a §1.10;
the reason `py_modules=[]` was added). And it is the only part of such an install that needs the network.

snp skips the install when the hook is local and has no `additional_dependencies` (04a Q11), with uv and with the pip
backend alike; with dependencies the uv backend installs only the dependencies and the pip backend keeps pre-commit's
`. *deps`. The environment, its interpreter, its seeded pip and the hook's activation are unchanged; the only trace is
that the distribution `pre-commit-placeholder-package` is absent from the environment, which no hook can sensibly
depend on.

##### Examples

A local python hook without dependencies that lists the distributions named like the placeholder
(`tests/differential/divergences/D-PERF-02.yaml`):

pre-commit 4.6.2, exit 0 (the four install lines, then):

```
placeholder..............................................................Passed
- hook id: placeholder
- duration: 0.03s

['pre_commit_placeholder_package']
```

snp, exit 0:

```
placeholder..............................................................Passed
- hook id: placeholder
- duration: 0.01s

[]
```

### D-PERF-03

native implementations (fast path, ADR-031); output byte-identical; Tier A repos are never cloned (FD-8)

* **Class:** PERF (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| pre-commit-hooks run from a cloned venv | native implementations (fast path, ADR-031); output byte-identical; Tier A repos are never cloned (FD-8) |

*The rationale and examples of this divergence are not written yet; the register entry above is
normative.*

### D-PERF-04

skipped when the tagged image exists (SNP_DOCKER_ALWAYS_BUILD=1 restores it)

* **Class:** PERF (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.6)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| docker hooks run `docker build` every run | skipped when the tagged image exists (`SNP_DOCKER_ALWAYS_BUILD=1` restores it) |

##### Rationale

pre-commit builds a `language: docker` hook repository's image at install time (`docker build --tag <tag> --label
PRE_COMMIT --pull .`) and then, because users prune images, rebuilds it before **every** hook run without `--pull`
(`docker.py:159-171`: "Rebuild the docker image in case it has gone missing"). With a warm build cache the rebuild is
a no-op that still costs a docker client start, a build-context upload of the whole hook repository and the daemon's
cache walk, per docker hook and per run — the dominant cost of a warm run that has docker hooks.

snp asks the daemon first: the per-run step is `docker build --tag <tag> --label PRE_COMMIT .` in the hook repository
(pre-commit's argv, cwd and environment) with the skip probe `docker image inspect <tag>`. When the probe succeeds the
image exists and the build is skipped; when it fails (image pruned, daemon error) the build runs exactly as in
pre-commit, and its failure is pre-commit's `CalledProcessError`.

Skipping is equivalent because the inputs of the build cannot have changed since the image was made: the build context
is the immutable checkout of the hook repository at a fixed `rev` (snp's prefixes are never modified after the
install, ADR-025), the per-run build never passes `--pull`, and its output was never shown. The one precondition is
that the tag names *this* repository's image: pre-commit's tag is `pre-commit-<md5(basename(prefix))>`, and because
every snp prefix is named `src` snp hashes the store's repository key instead (ADR-035), so two repositories never
share a tag and the probe cannot find another repository's image. What a skip can miss is a base image that was
re-tagged upstream since the install — which pre-commit's `pull=False` rebuild does not pick up either, since the cached
layers are reused.

`SNP_DOCKER_ALWAYS_BUILD` (set, non-empty, not `0`/`false`) drops the probe and restores pre-commit's unconditional
rebuild, e.g. for local Dockerfiles whose `ADD` of remote URLs should be re-evaluated on every run.

##### Examples

A local `docker` hook run twice with a fake `docker` that logs its verbs
(`tests/differential/divergences/D-PERF-04.yaml`). Both tools print the same transcript and exit 0:

```
[INFO] Initializing environment for local.
[INFO] Installing environment for local.
[INFO] Once installed this environment will be reused.
[INFO] This may take a few minutes...
fake docker..............................................................Passed
fake docker..............................................................Passed
```

The fake docker's log differs. pre-commit 4.6.2 (recorded with `pc462-py312`):

```
build --pull
build
run
build
run
```

snp:

```
build --pull
image inspect
run
image inspect
run
```

With `SNP_DOCKER_ALWAYS_BUILD=1`, snp's log equals pre-commit's.

## 5.7 EXT — observable only when an snp extension is used

### D-EXT-01

recognised extension keys (§7) produce no Unexpected key(s) warning and take effect

* **Class:** EXT (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| recognised extension keys (§7) produce no `Unexpected key(s)` warning and take effect |

##### Rationale

snp's extension keys (COMPATIBILITY §7) are plain keys a config shares with pre-commit (ADR-039). pre-commit treats
them as unknown keys: root keys print `Unexpected key(s) present at root: …` when the config loads, hook keys print
`Unexpected key(s) present on <src> => <id>: …` when the hooks are built, and nothing else changes. snp recognises
them: they are validated (with pre-commit's contexts and snp leaves, appended after pre-commit's items so every
pre-commit error and warning keeps its order) and take effect, and they produce no warning.

The difference is observable only in a config that uses an extension key. Unknown keys — including `x-*` keys and
extension keys inside a manifest — keep pre-commit's warnings byte for byte, and `SNP_COMPAT_STRICT=1`
(`ExtMode::Strict`) makes snp treat every extension key exactly as pre-commit does (the differential harness's
mode).

##### Examples

```yaml
priorities: {early: 1}
repos:
-   repo: local
    hooks:
    -   id: fmt
        name: fmt
        entry: echo fmt
        language: system
        priority: early
        groups: [fast]
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 `run --all-files` prints `[WARNING] Unexpected key(s) present at root: priorities` and
`[WARNING] Unexpected key(s) present on local => fmt: groups, priority` before the hook line. snp prints only the
hook line (and with `SNP_COMPAT_STRICT=1` prints both warnings exactly like pre-commit).

### D-EXT-02

the local overlay .pre-commit-config.local.yaml / SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG

* **Class:** EXT (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| the local overlay `.pre-commit-config.local.yaml` / `SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG` |

##### Rationale

lefthook's `lefthook-local.yml` (05 §18.4 A3) gives every developer a git-ignored file for personal tweaks —
skip a slow hook, wrap an entry in `docker compose run`, set an environment variable — without editing the shared
config; pre-commit's only escape hatch is `SKIP=`. snp reads `<config dir>/.pre-commit-config.local.yaml` (or
`.yml`, or the file named by `SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG`) and applies it on top of the config: root items (`skip_groups`,
`fail_on_changes`, appended `repos`) to the `Config`, hook entries keyed by alias or id after the manifest ∪
config merge, so `{entry}` expands against the merged entry of remote hooks too and the patched hook is what the
fast path and the install key see (ARCHITECTURE §8.4).

pre-commit never reads the file. The overlay is ignored when it is tracked by git (it is per developer by
definition) or when `CI` is truthy unless named explicitly, and `SNP_COMPAT_STRICT=1` disables it, so shared and CI
runs behave exactly like the config alone. Its use is always announced on stderr (D-EXT-03).

##### Examples

`.pre-commit-config.local.yaml` (untracked) next to a config with a local `pytest` hook:

```yaml
hooks:
  pytest:
    entry: docker compose run --rm app {entry}
    args: [-x]
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 runs `pytest -q …` as configured. snp prints `snp: using local overrides from
.pre-commit-config.local.yaml` on stderr and runs `docker compose run --rm app pytest -q -x …`.

### D-EXT-03

local-overlay notices on stderr: snp: using local overrides from {path}, the ignored-overlay note (tracked by git / CI), snp: local config overrides unknown…

* **Class:** EXT (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| local-overlay notices on stderr: `snp: using local overrides from {path}`, the ignored-overlay note (tracked by git / CI), `snp: local config overrides unknown hook '<id>'` |

##### Rationale

A per-developer overlay silently changing what a commit runs would make "works on my machine" bugs invisible,
so every effect of the overlay is announced — on stderr only, so stdout (hook lines, warnings, CI greps) stays
pre-commit's. The lines exist only when an overlay file exists next to the config or `SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG` names one;
a repository without an overlay prints nothing new.

##### Examples

* active: `snp: using local overrides from .pre-commit-config.local.yaml`
* tracked by git: `snp: ignoring local config .pre-commit-config.local.yaml: it is tracked by git (local overrides
  are per developer; untrack it or name it in SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG)`
* CI: `snp: ignoring local config .pre-commit-config.local.yaml: CI is set (name it in SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG to use it in
  CI)`
* `SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG` names a missing file: `snp: ignoring local config <path>: SNP_LOCAL_CONFIG names a file that does
  not exist`
* an overlay hook matching no hook: `snp: local config overrides unknown hook 'nonexistent'`

pre-commit 4.6.2 prints none of these (it never reads the overlay).

### D-EXT-04

_SNP_STASH_LOCK=<token> is exported to hooks while a stash is held (nested runs skip the worktree lock) — class DATA

* **Class:** DATA (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| `_SNP_STASH_LOCK=<token>` is exported to hooks while a stash is held (nested runs skip the worktree lock) — class DATA |

##### Rationale

The worktree lock of D-DATA-13 would deadlock a hook that itself runs snp in the same worktree (a wrapper hook, a
`snp run` inside a `make` target, `snp try-repo` from a hook): the nested run would wait for the lock its parent holds
until it times out. pre-commit has no lock, and its nested run simply sees the stashed (clean) worktree.

snp therefore exports one extra variable to hooks while its guard is alive: `_SNP_STASH_LOCK=<token>`, a random
128-bit hex token that is also written into the held lock file. A run that finds the lock held **and** its own
`_SNP_STASH_LOCK` equal to the file's token skips the lock and behaves as pre-commit's nested run does; a token that
matches a released lock (left behind by a crash) exempts nobody, and releasing the lock truncates the token. The name
starts with an underscore like pre-commit's own `_PRE_COMMIT_SKIP_POST_CHECKOUT`. It is class DATA (not EXT) because it
is always on and exists to protect the stash.

Why it is safe: one additional environment variable is visible to hooks; nothing else about the hook environment
(02 §6.1) changes, and no hook relies on the absence of an underscore-prefixed snp variable.

##### Examples

```text
$ cat .pre-commit-config.yaml   # a hook that prints its environment
…  entry: sh -c 'env | grep _SNP_STASH_LOCK' --
$ pre-commit run --verbose
(nothing printed by the hook; it fails because grep finds nothing)
$ snp run --verbose
_SNP_STASH_LOCK=5f0c…e21a                     (32 hex digits)
```

Proof: `crates/snp-stash/tests/behaviour/guard.rs::{nested_run_with_the_token_proceeds_while_the_lock_is_held,
stale_token_in_a_released_lock_file_exempts_nobody}`; the scenario `tests/differential/divergences/D-EXT-04.yaml`.

### D-EXT-05

SNP=0/false makes hook-impl skip snp's hooks (the legacy hook still runs)

* **Class:** EXT (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| `SNP=0`/`false` makes `hook-impl` skip snp's hooks (the legacy hook still runs) |

*The rationale and examples of this divergence are not written yet; the register entry above is
normative.*

### D-EXT-06

repo: builtin (pre-commit rejects these configs)

* **Class:** EXT (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| `repo: builtin` (pre-commit rejects these configs) |

##### Rationale

`- repo: builtin` runs pre-commit-hooks' hooks natively without cloning anything (ARCHITECTURE §7.3). pre-commit
treats `builtin` as a remote URL and rejects the entry (`Missing required key: rev`, or a clone failure with a
rev), so such a config is snp-only by construction; COMPATIBILITY §7.3 documents it as an extension that is not
portable, and `snp migrate builtin` / `snp migrate upstream` convert both ways.

The validation is part of the config schema as cfgv items with cfgv contexts, so `validate-config` and `run` agree:
no `rev`; `entry` and `additional_dependencies` cannot be set; `language` is absent or `system`; every other hook
key and every extension key is checked like a remote config hook. The items for other repo kinds are unchanged
(pre-commit's remote-repo items skip only `builtin`), so no pre-commit message changes, and in `ExtMode::Strict`
`builtin` is an ordinary remote repo exactly as in pre-commit.

##### Examples

```yaml
repos:
-   repo: builtin
    hooks:
    -   id: trailing-whitespace
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 `validate-config`, exit **1**:

```

==> File .pre-commit-config.yaml
==> At Config()
==> At key: repos
==> At Repository(repo='builtin')
=====> Missing required key: rev
```

snp: valid (exit 0); `rev: v6.0.0` added to it gives `=====> Expected rev to be absent when repo is 'builtin',
found rev: 'v6.0.0'`, `entry: x` gives `=====> 'entry' cannot be overridden` under `At Hook(id=…)`.

### D-EXT-07

snp-brand commands and flags (§8), including their presence in the snp brand's usage/help blocks

* **Class:** EXT (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.7)

| Divergence |
|---|
| snp-brand commands and flags (§8), including their presence in the snp brand's usage/help blocks |

##### Rationale

The snp brand adds the extensions of COMPATIBILITY §8.1 / ARCHITECTURE §9.3 to pre-commit's parser tree:

| Parser | Additions |
|---|---|
| top level | commands `cache`, `completions`, `config`, `doctor`, `list`, `migrate`, `self` (inserted alphabetically; `help` and `hook-impl` stay last) |
| `run`, `try-repo` | several hook ids (`hook` is `nargs='*'`; `:` allowed), `-j/--jobs`, `--group`, `--require-group`, `--no-group`, `--no-fast-path`, `--stdin-files[=nul\|lines]` (a third member of the `--all-files \| --files` group), `--summary`, `--no-local-config` |
| `install`, `uninstall` | `--git-config-hooks` (ADR-057) |
| `install-hooks` | `--with-fallback` |
| `validate-config`, `validate-manifest` | `--strict`, `--portable` |

They change the usage and help blocks of those parsers (new options, a longer `{…}` command list), the
`invalid choice` list of the top-level parser and of course what is accepted.

Why it is safe:

* **Only the snp brand has them.** Under the `pre-commit` name the parser tree is exactly pre-commit's
  (`PRE_COMMIT_SPEC`): every extension is rejected with pre-commit's own texts (`invalid choice: 'list' (choose from
  …)`, `unrecognized arguments: --summary`), byte-identical to pre-commit 4.6.2 (`compat.json` goldens).
* **No existing command line changes meaning.** `snp_argparse::prefix_stable(PRE_COMMIT_SPEC, SNP_SPEC)` checks that
  every long-option abbreviation pre-commit resolves uniquely resolves to the same option in the snp brand
  (`run --all`, `run --fi`, `install --conf x.yaml`, …); the planted names `--files-from-stdin` and `--config-hooks` fail
  it (ADR-057, ARCHITECTURE §9.2). The extensions only turn pre-commit's usage errors into accepted command lines:
  `run a b` (two hook ids) instead of `unrecognized arguments: b`.
* **The texts are argparse's.** The snp-brand usage/help/error blocks of the parsers that carry extensions are
  rendered by `snp_argparse` and golden-tested against a real CPython 3.13.14 argparse built from
  `export_json(SNP_SPEC, "snp")` (ADR-058; `crates/snp-cli/tests/goldens/snp.json`).

argparse semantics apply to the extensions too: `--stdin-files` takes an optional value, so a hook id must not follow
it directly (`snp run --stdin-files hook` → `invalid choice: 'hook'`); write `snp run hook --stdin-files` or
`--stdin-files=lines hook`. Unknown options are still deferred to the top level, and hook ids interleaved with
options follow argparse's positional rules (`snp run a -a b` → `unrecognized arguments: b`).

##### Examples

```text
$ pre-commit list
usage: pre-commit [-h] [-V]
                  {autoupdate,clean,gc,hazmat,init-templatedir,install,install-hooks,migrate-config,run,sample-config,try-repo,uninstall,validate-config,validate-manifest,help,hook-impl} ...
pre-commit: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'list' (choose from 'autoupdate', 'clean', 'gc', 'hazmat', 'init-templatedir', 'install', 'install-hooks', 'migrate-config', 'run', 'sample-config', 'try-repo', 'uninstall', 'validate-config', 'validate-manifest', 'help', 'hook-impl')
$ snp list            # accepted: Cli::List
```

```text
$ pre-commit run --bogus
usage: pre-commit [-h] [-V]
                  {autoupdate,clean,gc,hazmat,init-templatedir,install,install-hooks,migrate-config,run,sample-config,try-repo,uninstall,validate-config,validate-manifest,help,hook-impl} ...
pre-commit: error: unrecognized arguments: --bogus
$ snp run --bogus
usage: snp [-h] [-V]
           {autoupdate,cache,clean,completions,config,doctor,gc,hazmat,init-templatedir,install,install-hooks,list,migrate,migrate-config,run,sample-config,self,try-repo,uninstall,validate-config,validate-manifest,help,hook-impl} ...
snp: error: unrecognized arguments: --bogus
```

`snp run -h` (usage block; pre-commit's has no `--stdin-files`, `-j` … `--no-local-config`, and `[hook]` instead of
`[hook ...]`):

```text
usage: snp run [-h] [--color {auto,always,never}] [-c CONFIG] [--verbose]
               [--all-files | --files [FILES ...] |
               --stdin-files [{nul,lines}]] [--show-diff-on-failure]
               [--fail-fast]
               …
               [--rewrite-command REWRITE_COMMAND] [-j JOBS] [--group GROUP]
               [--require-group GROUP] [--no-group GROUP] [--no-fast-path]
               [--summary] [--no-local-config]
               [hook ...]
```

The scenario `tests/differential/divergences/D-EXT-07.yaml` runs `snp -h`, `snp run -h` and `snp run a b` against the
oracle, where they must keep differing.

## 5.8 DIAG — always-on stderr diagnostics (stdout and exit codes unchanged)

### D-DIAG-01

git < 2.31: `[WARNING] git <V> is older than 2.31.0, the oldest git version snp is tested with. Set SNP_ALLOW_OLD_GIT=1 to silence this warning.` (once per process; 02 G.4)

* **Class:** DIAG (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

| ID | Diagnostic (stderr only) | WP |
|---|---|---|
| D-DIAG-01 | git < 2.31: `[WARNING] git <V> is older than 2.31.0, the oldest git version snp is tested with. Set SNP_ALLOW_OLD_GIT=1 to silence this warning.` (once per process; 02 G.4) | 18 |

##### Rationale

pre-commit 4.6.2 has no git version check, yet needs git ≥ 2.31 for `ls-files --deduplicate` and ≥ 2.19 for
intent-to-add detection in the stash (02 G.0 item 1). snp never refuses a git (ADR-063: below 2.31 it falls back —
D-CRASH-26 — and only a stash that would need intent-to-add detection is refused below 2.19, D-DATA-17), but a user on
a warning-band git runs combinations snp's CI tests only as smoke tests (Debian 11's 2.30.2, Ubuntu 20.04's 2.25.1).
One stderr line per process says so and how to silence it; stdout and the exit code stay byte-identical to
pre-commit, so the line is a DIAG divergence (always on, stderr only).

The version comes from `git --version` (`git version 2.30.2` → `2.30.2`; suffixes such as `(Apple Git-154)`,
`.windows.2`, `.rc0` ignored; an unparseable version is treated as the newest and never warns). `[WARNING]` is
coloured like pre-commit's log lines when colour is on (`\x1b[43;30m[WARNING]\x1b[m`). The text names snp in both
brands. `SNP_ALLOW_OLD_GIT` set to any non-empty value silences it.

##### Examples

`pre-commit run` (compat alias) on Debian 11 (git 2.30.2), a staged file and a passing hook.

pre-commit 4.6.2: stdout `x........Passed`, no stderr, exit 0.

snp: the same stdout bytes and exit 0; stderr:

```
[WARNING] git 2.30.2 is older than 2.31.0, the oldest git version snp is tested with. Set SNP_ALLOW_OLD_GIT=1 to silence this warning.
```

With `SNP_ALLOW_OLD_GIT=1`: no stderr — byte-identical to pre-commit.

Regression tests: `crates/snp-git/tests/behaviour/exe.rs` `version_gate_never_refuses_and_warns_once` (exactly one
line on stderr for repeated calls, none with `SNP_ALLOW_OLD_GIT=1`, none for ≥ 2.31 or an unparseable version,
nothing on stdout), `messages::tests::old_git_warning_both_brands_and_colours`, and the version-parser table
`exe::tests::version_parser_table`. The scenario runs on the CI git 2.30 container.

install/uninstall/init-templatedir/doctor --fix notes when replacing other managers' scripts: M1 Replaced hook script from {owner} at {hook_path} [+ (Python:…

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

| Diagnostic (stderr only) |
|---|
| `install`/`uninstall`/`init-templatedir`/`doctor --fix` notes when replacing other managers' scripts: M1 `Replaced hook script from {owner} at {hook_path}` [+ ` (Python: {INSTALL_PYTHON})`], M1b, M2 `Removed {legacy_path}: it is a hook script from {owner}, not a user hook`, M3 ``Note: {hook_path} still runs {owner}; run `{prog} install -t {T}` to switch it to snp``, M12 (11 §A.5.4) — both brands |

run hint, only when stderr is a TTY, SNP_NO_HINTS unset/empty and core.hooksPath unset: hint: {hook_path} runs {owner}, not snp; run {prog} install to switch…

| Diagnostic (stderr only) |

| `run` hint, only when stderr is a TTY, `SNP_NO_HINTS` unset/empty and `core.hooksPath` unset: ``hint: {hook_path} runs {owner}, not snp; run `{prog} install` to switch`` (11 §A.14) |

### D-DIAG-04

stash notices: the next-run recovery notice (§4.6), snp: waiting for another snp run in this worktree…, snp: restoring stashed changes, please wait, snp: git…

* **Class:** DIAG (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

| Diagnostic (stderr only) |
|---|
| stash notices: the next-run recovery notice (§4.6), `snp: waiting for another snp run in this worktree…`, `snp: restoring stashed changes, please wait`, `snp: git needed the terminal during the restore and was stopped` |

##### Rationale

Each notice reports a situation pre-commit cannot be in (it has no lock, journal, signal handler or isolated restore)
or handles silently to the user's loss:

* **recovery notice** — an earlier run never restored; where the work is and the command that restores it
  (D-DATA-13, ARCHITECTURE §4.6). Printed by the next stash in the worktree, once per orphaned journal.
* **`snp: waiting for another snp run in this worktree…`** — printed once when the worktree lock is contended
  (D-DATA-13), so a waiting commit does not look hung.
* **`snp: restoring stashed changes, please wait`** — printed once when a further signal arrives while the restore
  runs under the `RestoreShield` (D-DATA-02): the restore is never abandoned, the user learns why snp does not exit.
* **`snp: git needed the terminal during the restore and was stopped`** — a restore command (e.g. a git-lfs credential
  prompt) read the terminal from its own process group and was stopped by SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU; snp kills it and continues
  with the rollback / K+ path (ADR-065), so the run cannot hang forever on an invisible prompt.

All of them name snp in both brands (snp-only diagnostics, COMPATIBILITY §5.8), go to stderr only, and never change
stdout or the exit code.

##### Examples

```text
snp: waiting for another snp run in this worktree…
snp: restoring stashed changes, please wait
snp: git needed the terminal during the restore and was stopped
snp: an earlier run was interrupted before it restored your unstaged changes; they are saved in /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218 (index tree 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904). Restore with: git --literal-pathspecs checkout 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 -- foo && git apply --3way /s/patches/patch1791403656-1781218 && git --literal-pathspecs reset -q 4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904 -- foo
```

Proof: `crates/snp-stash/src/messages.rs` (goldens), `tests/behaviour/guard.rs::{concurrent_second_run_waits_once_…,
a_tty_stopped_restore_is_reported_…}`, `tests/driver.rs::a_second_ctrl_c_during_git_apply_never_interrupts_it`
(exactly one restore notice). The scenario `tests/differential/divergences/D-DIAG-04.yaml` provokes the recovery
notice (the other three need concurrency or signals and are covered by the process tests).

### D-DIAG-05

store notices: the foreign-owner warning (ADR-044), `Removed snp 1.x cache data from {store}.` (gc)

* **Class:** DIAG (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.8)

| Diagnostic (stderr only) |
|---|
| store notices: the foreign-owner warning (ADR-044), `Removed snp 1.x cache data from {store}.` (gc) |

##### Rationale

Two stderr-only notices of snp's own store, which pre-commit cannot print because it has no such situations:

* **Foreign owner** (ADR-044): `[WARNING] the snp store <path> is owned by uid <n>, not by the current user` — once
  per process, from `Store::ensure_created`, when the store belongs to another uid and is used anyway (volume-mounted
  CI caches; as root only with `SNP_ALLOW_FOREIGN_STORE=1`, D-SEC-13).
* **snp 1.x leftovers** (11 §A.10.3): snp 1.x used `~/.cache/snp` with `db.db`, `repos/`, `environments/` and
  `resource-pools/`. `Store::sweep` (gc) removes them only when the store's README carries the 1.x signature (`This
  directory is maintained by the SNP (Shell Not Pass) project.`), rewrites the README and reports
  `SweepReport::legacy_v1_removed`; WP-33's `gc` then prints `Removed snp 1.x cache data from {store}.` on stderr
  before `{n} repo(s) removed.`.

Safe: stderr only; stdout and exit codes are unchanged.

##### Examples

`gc` with `SNP_HOME` pointing at a directory that holds an snp 1.x README and `db.db`
(`tests/differential/divergences/D-DIAG-05.yaml`). pre-commit 4.6.2 (its own store), exit 0, stdout
`0 repo(s) removed.`, empty stderr. snp, exit 0, the same stdout and on stderr:

```text
Removed snp 1.x cache data from <W>/snpstore.
```

Unit coverage: `crates/snp-store/tests/support/behaviour.rs::sweep_removes_other_versions_and_snp1_leftovers`;
the foreign-owner text is golden-tested in `crates/snp-store/src/messages.rs`.

## 5.9 TIERB — Python-internal bytes

### D-MISC-04

one stderr line per distinct (pattern, warning): [WARNING] regex {pattern!r}: {msg} (Python FutureWarning); SNP_PYTHON_WARNINGS=0 silences

* **Class:** TIERB (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| regex `FutureWarning` lines: `…/cfgv.py:386: FutureWarning: Possible nested set at position 1` + `  re.compile(v)` on stderr | one stderr line per distinct (pattern, warning): `[WARNING] regex {pattern!r}: {msg} (Python FutureWarning)`; `SNP_PYTHON_WARNINGS=0` silences |

##### Rationale

CPython 3.7+ emits a `FutureWarning` while compiling a `files`/`exclude` pattern that would change meaning under
future set syntax (`[[`, `&&`, `||`, `~~`, `--` inside a class). Python's warnings machinery prints it on stderr as
two lines naming the interpreter's site-packages path and the source line (`…/cfgv.py:386: FutureWarning:
Possible nested set at position 1` / `  re.compile(v)`), once per process and message text; `PYTHONWARNINGS`
controls it. Those bytes cannot be reproduced without Python (TIERB).

snp keeps the information and drops the interpreter noise: it prints one stderr line per distinct (pattern,
message), `[WARNING] regex {pattern!r}: {msg} (Python FutureWarning)`, with CPython 3.12's message and position
(snp-pyre). The lines come in the order pre-commit compiles the patterns (cfgv item order: a config's
`repos` and their hooks before the top-level `files` / `exclude`), and — like pre-commit, which compiles them
during validation — also when a later item makes validation fail. Two residual differences: Python prints a
message text once per process (a second pattern with the same message is silent), snp once per pattern; and
a pattern that fails to compile (`[a--b]`, a bad range CPython warns about before raising `re.error`) gets
only its validation error. stdout and the exit code are unchanged; the pattern keeps Python's literal
semantics; `PYTHONWARNINGS` has no effect on snp's line (X13-SM-10) and is passed through to hooks unchanged.

##### Examples

```yaml
files: '[[]'
repos: []
```

pre-commit 4.6.2 `validate-config`, exit 0, stderr:

```
<site-packages>/cfgv.py:386: FutureWarning: Possible nested set at position 1
  re.compile(v)
```

snp, exit 0, stderr:

```
[WARNING] regex '[[]': Possible nested set at position 1 (Python FutureWarning)
```

### D-MISC-05

An invalid pygrep entry fails the hook once, with the last line of Python's traceback.

* **Class:** MISC (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)
* **Catalog:** 01 Addendum §A.4.5, X13-EXE-07 (13 X.4.5); tests `x13_exe_07_non_re_error_entries` and the
  `invalid-*` rows of `pygrep_goldens` (`crates/snp-hooks/tests/pygrep/main.rs`).

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| invalid pygrep entry: one full traceback per xargs partition | one line in Python's form (`re.error: … at position N`), exit 1 |

##### Rationale

pre-commit runs `python -m pre_commit.languages.pygrep *args entry *files` once per xargs partition, and the entry is
never validated as a regex (`entry` is not a `check_regex` key). An entry that `re.compile` rejects therefore prints a
complete Python traceback — about ten lines naming the interpreter's own files — **once per partition**: 19 identical
tracebacks for 40 000 files (01 Addendum §A.4.5). Each ends in the same line: `re.PatternError: missing ),
unterminated subpattern at position 0` on CPython 3.13 (`re.error: …` up to 3.12), `OverflowError: the repetition
number is too large`, `ValueError: ASCII and LOCALE flags are incompatible`, `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth
exceeded`. The hook fails with `- exit code: 1`.

The native compiles the pattern once per hook per run (`pygrep::prepare`) and reports an invalid one once, as that
final line plus a newline, exit 1, without touching any file. The pass/fail result and the exit code are pre-commit's;
the error text is the part of pre-commit's output that identifies the problem; what is dropped are the
machine-specific frames and the repetitions. The tracebacks cannot be byte-identical in any case (they contain the
user's venv paths), so this is a Tier B message difference (01 Addendum §A.4.5 "snp rule"). The class name follows the
emulated CPython 3.13 (`re.PatternError`); the message text and its `at position N` / `(line L, column C)` suffix are
CPython's exactly (snp-pyre).

##### Examples

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` with a local hook `id: grep`, `language: pygrep`, `entry: '('`, run on a repository whose
file list makes two xargs partitions:

pre-commit 4.6.2 (`- exit code: 1`):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  …
re.PatternError: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  …
re.PatternError: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0
```

snp (`- exit code: 1`):

```
re.PatternError: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0
```

The scenario in `tests/differential/divergences/D-MISC-05.yaml` runs this hook over enough files for several
partitions.

##### Related hook-time regex messages (pygrep, no-commit-to-branch)

Two further hook-time regex texts of the natives follow from the same rule (the problem is reported in snp's own
one-line form because Python's text names interpreter files). Until the integration lead extends the register row
(D-MISC-04 covers only cfgv's config-time warnings), they are documented here:

* **`FutureWarning`s** (`[[`, `[a&&b]`, …). Python writes
  `<site-packages>/pre_commit/languages/pygrep.py:123: FutureWarning: Possible nested set at position 1` plus the
  source line `  pattern = re.compile(args.pattern.encode(), flags)` to stderr, which the runner merges into the
  hook output, once per process (once per xargs partition); no-commit-to-branch prints
  `…/no_commit_to_branch.py:23: FutureWarning: …` plus `  re.match(p, branch_name) for p in patterns` for each
  pattern it compiles. snp writes the D-MISC-04 form at the same place in the output (before any match line):
  `[WARNING] regex '[[x]': Possible nested set at position 1 (Python FutureWarning)`. no-commit-to-branch honours
  `SNP_PYTHON_WARNINGS=0`; `pygrep::run_partition` has no environment in its frozen signature (ARCH §1.4.19), so
  pygrep always prints them. Exit codes and match lines are unchanged.
* **Backtracking limit** (D-SEC-10). A pattern that exceeds snp-pyre's limit (CPython would hang) ends the
  partition with `snp: regular expression {pattern!r} exceeded the backtracking limit on {path!r}`, exit 1, after
  the match lines printed so far. no-commit-to-branch fails **closed** the same way (`… on {branch!r}`, exit 1): a
  hanging CPython never let the commit through either.

### D-MISC-06

Regular-expression corner cases where snp's engines cannot reproduce CPython 3.12 `re` exactly (01 Addendum
§A.6.13 D1–D6, plus D7–D8 found in the WP-13 review and pending a §A.6.13 / COMPATIBILITY row update by the
integration lead). None occurs in the 4 858-pattern corpus.

* **Class:** TIERB (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| regex corner cases (01 Addendum §A.6.13 D1–D6): IGNORECASE backreferences across `K`/`k`, `ſ`/`s`, `ς`/`σ`; code points unassigned in UCD 15.0 treated as UCD 16; `\N{…}` without the `py-re-names` feature; `(?L)` under a single-byte non-UTF-8 locale; patterns too large for the engines (`Unsupported`, reported as the validation error plus a stderr hint); D7: `\U` above 0x7FFFFFFF in a str pattern (`OverflowError` in CPython, `bad escape` in snp); D8: nullable loop bodies that are bounded, possessive, or `{2,}` with captures a back-reference or conditional observes | as stated (corpus frequency 0) |

##### Rationale

snp parses every pattern with an exact port of CPython 3.12's `re/_parser.py` (accept/reject, message, position
and `FutureWarning`s equal CPython on every committed vector) and lowers it to explicit `regex` / `fancy-regex`
syntax. Matching is then exact except where the engines themselves differ, which the lowering cannot paper over
without a third, backtracking engine of snp's own:

* **D1 — IGNORECASE back-references.** CPython compares a back-reference under IGNORECASE character by character
  with `lower(a) == lower(b)` and without its `_EXTRA_CASES` table; fancy-regex compares simple case folds of equal
  UTF-8 length. So `(?i)(k)\1` matches `kK` (U+212A KELVIN SIGN, 3 bytes) in CPython but not in snp, and
  `(?i)(σ)\1` matches `σς` in snp but not in CPython (likewise `ſ`/`s`, `İ`, and the Latin-1 lane of bytes
  patterns for U+00C0–U+00FE). 40 of 18 382 fuzzed patterns, 0 corpus patterns; every other IGNORECASE construct is
  lowered to explicit classes and is exact (`crates/snp-pyre/tests/vectors.rs` tolerates exactly these rows).
* **D2 — Unicode version.** Python 3.12 ships UCD 15.0; `regex-syntax` ships UCD 16. Code points assigned only in
  16.0 are `\w` / case pairs in snp (as in Python 3.14) — the delta is allow-listed in `src/tests.rs`.
* **D3 — `\N{…}` without the `py-re-names` feature** (default on, ≈ 1.3 MB of names): `PyReError::Unsupported`.
* **D4 — `(?L)`** on bytes patterns follows the C/UTF-8 locale (no byte ≥ 0x80 is alphanumeric or cased); under a
  single-byte locale such as `de_DE.ISO-8859-1` CPython would follow the locale's `isalnum`.
* **D5 / D6 — engine limits.** A repeat count that unrolls past the 64 MiB `regex` size budget (`a{100000}`), or a
  backtracking (tier-2) pattern nested 64 or more groups deep, compiles in CPython but is `Unsupported` in snp,
  reported as cfgv's `… is not a valid python regex` validation error plus a stderr hint — never a crash, never a
  silent mismatch.

* **D7 — `\U` past a C int.** In a str pattern `\U80000000` … `\UFFFFFFFF` (also inside a set) makes `chr()` in
  `re/_parser.py` raise `OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C int` instead of the `re.error`
  `bad escape \U…` of the values 0x110000–0x7FFFFFFF. snp reports the `bad escape` (position included):
  `snp_pyre::PyReError::Overflow` carries the fixed repetition text, and a message-carrying variant would change
  the frozen ARCH §1.4.5 contract. Both are rejections; only pygrep's last traceback line differs (and the class
  pre-commit would crash with on a config pattern, D-CRASH-04). Bytes patterns have no `\U` escape and are exact.
  The edge vectors carry the three shapes; `tests/vectors.rs` tolerates exactly this class.
* **D8 — empty iterations snp cannot end like `MAX_UNTIL`.** CPython leaves a loop after an iteration that matched
  the empty string, with that iteration's priority (`_sre` `last_ptr`). snp runs unbounded greedy loops over a
  nullable body on fancy-regex's epsilon-checked VM loop (and `X{m,}` as `X{m}` + such a loop), which is exact
  (`(?:x*|y)+` on `xyx` is `(0, 1)`, as `pygrep --multiline` needs). Left: bounded `X{m,n}` and possessive loops over
  a nullable body, and `X{m,}` (m ≥ 2) when a back-reference or conditional can observe X's captures. There the match
  *end* may differ (never whether `re.search` finds a match), and a conditional on a group of the loop can see an
  iteration CPython never runs: `(?x)((a)?(?<!\n)(?(1)[a-z]|(?:i|^))){0,2}` fullmatches `ab` in snp, not in CPython
  (this is the "conditional re-entry" class of `gen_re_vectors.py`, about one random pattern in 4 000). The same
  span difference remains for a tier-1 pattern nested 63 or more groups deep, whose exact form fancy-regex cannot
  build.

All eight are safe: they are deterministic, need deliberately exotic patterns, and either fail loudly (D3, D5, D6, D7: a
rejected pattern stays rejected) or change the answer only for case-insensitive back-references between rare
letters (D1), for characters newer than UCD 15.0 (D2), or for empty iterations of exotic nullable loops (D8).

Fixed in the WP-13 review (exact now, with regression tests in `crates/snp-pyre/tests/acceptance.rs` and edge
vectors): spans of unbounded nullable loops; fancy-regex 0.19's tree rewrites of lazy bodies (`(X+?)*` → `(X+?)?`,
`a*b??a*` → `a*(?:ba*)?`); the search-only charset prefix of a leading scoped `(?a:…)` set (`re.search(r'(?a:\W)',
'é')` is `None` while `re.match` matches); and pygrep's own recursion depth for bytes patterns (494 nested groups
compile, 495 raise `RecursionError`, against 484/485 for config patterns).

##### Examples

D1, the scenario of `tests/differential/divergences/D-MISC-06.yaml`: a local hook `language: fail`,
`entry: the files pattern matched`, `files: '(?i)(σ)\1'`; the repository holds the empty file `σς.txt`;
`run --all-files`.

pre-commit 4.6.2 (CPython 3.12.3: `re.search(r'(?i)(σ)\1', 'σς.txt')` is `None`; bytes captured with the same code
of pre-commit 4.1.0 on 3.12.3), exit 0:

```text
matched..............................................(no files to check)Skipped
```

snp (fancy-regex folds `ς` and `σ` to the same 2-byte `σ`, so the file matches), exit 1:

```text
matched..................................................................Failed
- hook id: matched
- exit code: 1

the files pattern matched

σς.txt

```

D5: `files: 'a{100000}'` — CPython compiles it; snp rejects the config with cfgv's
`=====> 'a{100000}' is not a valid python regex` and the hint `the pattern's repeat counts expand beyond the regular
expression engines' size budget`. D6: `files: '(((…(?=a)a…)))'` with 70 nested groups — CPython compiles it; snp
reports `the pattern nests too deeply for the backtracking engine (…)`.

### D-MISC-07

An in-hook hazmat failure prints only the final line of Python's traceback.

* **Class:** MISC (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)
* **Catalog:** X13-HZ-06 (13 X.4.9), 03 Addendum §H.5/§H.8.6; tests `x13_hz_06_in_hook_failures` and
  `hazmat_goldens` (`crates/snp-hooks/tests/hazmat/main.rs`).

##### Register entry (COMPATIBILITY §5.9)

| pre-commit 4.6.2 | snp |
|---|---|
| in-hook hazmat exec failure: full Python traceback | only the final traceback line (`pre_commit.parse_shebang.ExecutableNotFoundError: Executable `x` not found`) |

##### Rationale

An `entry: pre-commit hazmat …` is rewritten by `lang_base.hook_cmd` to `python -m pre_commit.commands.hazmat …`
(`lang_base.py:174-178`). That module has no error handler: when the command cannot be resolved (`not found`, `is a
directory`, `is not executable`), the command is empty (`IndexError`), the `cd` directory is missing
(`FileNotFoundError`) or the exec fails (`OSError: [Errno 8] Exec format error`), Python prints a full traceback into
the hook's output — 15 to 20 lines of frames naming the venv's absolute paths — and exits 1, once per xargs partition
(03 Addendum §H.5 A3–A7, B3–B13, C2–C8).

snp rewrites the same entries to `snp __hazmat …` (D-MISC-02), which reproduces the module's behaviour — the same
exit codes (1 for these failures, 2 for argparse errors with prog `hazmat.py`, the child's status otherwise, `n1`'s
OR, `-N & 0xFF` for signals), the same `SystemExit` texts and argparse texts — but prints only the last line of the
traceback, byte for byte: the line that names the problem (`pre_commit.parse_shebang.ExecutableNotFoundError:
Executable `nope-not-here` not found`). The frames cannot be reproduced (they are the user's interpreter paths and
line numbers of pre-commit's source), carry no information about the user's hook, and a fake `Traceback (most recent
call last):` header would be misleading. Pass/fail and exit codes are unchanged; the difference is confined to the
message block (Tier B, 03 Addendum §H.8.6).

##### Examples

A local hook `entry: pre-commit hazmat n1 nope-not-here --`, `language: system`, on one file:

pre-commit 4.6.2 (`- exit code: 1`):

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 88, in _run_code
  File "<site>/pre_commit/commands/hazmat.py", line 95, in <module>
    raise SystemExit(main())
  …
  File "<site>/pre_commit/parse_shebang.py", line 48, in _error
    raise ExecutableNotFoundError(f'Executable `{orig}` {msg}')
pre_commit.parse_shebang.ExecutableNotFoundError: Executable `nope-not-here` not found
```

snp (`- exit code: 1`):

```
pre_commit.parse_shebang.ExecutableNotFoundError: Executable `nope-not-here` not found
```

The scenario in `tests/differential/divergences/D-MISC-07.yaml` runs exactly this hook.
